- **一句话定义**：读 spec → 拆任务 → 写代码 → 自测 → 迭代的长循环 agent 命令，带停机守护。
- **命令形态**：`/ralph <spec-ref> [exclude=...] [include-only=...] [max-loops=N] [commit=off|per-task|per-milestone] [dry-run=true]`。
- **执行循环**：`INGEST → PLAN → PICK → ACT → VERIFY → UPDATE → (loop) → REPORT`，带 PAUSE 分支。
- **停机条件**：全部 todo 完成 / `max-loops` 用尽 / 破坏性操作或用户中止。

## PLAN — 写 TodoWrite

 我已经完整地盘点了所有现有的代码。按照规范分类，视觉动作识别部分是主要工作，包括一个完整的 YOLO-Pose 管道来处理多人姿态检测和追踪，以及一个坐标映射模块用于将 COCO 关键点转换为 MediaPipe 格式。

几何计算、深蹲检测和重复计数的状态机都已实现，还有额外的手势识别和 MediaPipe Hands 补强功能，但跳跃、拳击和高抬腿这些 P3 优先级的动作检测器还缺失，动作不匹配的反馈逻辑也还没有。BPM 估计和 IMU 适配部分已经有了基于重复时间戳的 BPM 计算器和反馈公式的实现。

现在看 IMU 部分，数据类、协议定义和虚拟适配器都还没有，频率到 BPM 的映射表和双路径估计器也缺失。Pure Data 的音粒引擎只有一个 OSC 转储，没有实现节拍器、表格读取和多轨道的主 kick 驱动。OSC 协议的发送器已经覆盖了车道的 BPM、相位、失谐和增益等参数，但缺少预期动作、动作警告和重复计数的消息。

课程文件、教学控制台、灯带和屏幕都超出了 MVP 范围。P1 验证需要多轨道音粒的 Pd 实现和虚拟多轨道发送器，而 P2 验证的姿态检测、深蹲识别和重复计数都已完成，还有网络摄像头预览和端到端烟雾测试。上层的编排器、轨道控制器和课程加载器都还没有实现，测试目录也是空的。

关于硬件排除项，我需要澄清的是 IMU 和手机适配器的软件抽象层是必须的——Protocol 定义、虚拟适配器和 OSC 桥接都属于软件层，不是硬件实装本身。SPEC 第 3 节 P1 阶段明确要求无硬件门槛，但交付物包括虚拟 IMU 实现；第 6.10 节整章讲的是硬件无关的适配器接口；没有 IMU Protocol，估计器就无法运行。所以我要做的是实现 Protocol、接口、虚拟适配器和 OSC 桥接这些软件抽象，但不写 ESP32 固件、真机手机适配器调用或灯带驱动——手机适配器可以先做骨架加虚拟数据测试，不依赖真机。

现在按照 SPEC 第 3 节 P1-P4 路线和第 8 节目录结构规划 17 个顶层任务，从 P1 缺口补齐开始。

Phase A 包括建立 IMU 包和 Protocol、实现虚拟适配器、添加频率到 BPM 的映射、升级 Pure Data 音频处理、搭建 OSC 桥接骨架和双路径 BPM 估计器，以及实现 IMU 加速度自相关的慢路径 BPM 检测。Phase B 扩展 OSC 协议以支持更多动作相关的地址。Phase C 则针对 P3 多动作识别，实现跳跃、拳击和高抬腿等动作的规则检测器。

Phase D 搭建编排层，包括课程文件加载、单 lane 控制和主进程编排。Phase E 补充单元测试和文档。我现在用 TodoWrite 记录这些任务，从 A1 开始执行，注意排除固件和视觉相关的目录，在 commit=off 模式下保留所有改动，单轮限制 20 个文件和 500 行变更。

```json
 "contents": "\"\"\"\nSPEC §6.10.1 unified IMU sample.\n\nA single ``IMUSample`` carries one frame of telemetry from any source —\nphone WebSocket, ESP32 wristband, AppleWatch, OSC bridge, or the\n:class:`python.imu.fake.FakeAdapter` used in P1 to drive the audio chain\nwithout any hardware at all.\n\nWhy one struct, not two\n-----------------------\nHardware splits naturally into \"raw acceleration\" devices (the spec's\n*mode A*) and \"frequency-only\" devices (*mode B* — DSP-on-MCU watches,\nSDK-only commercial bands). Some devices give both (*mode C*). Modelling\nall three with a single optional-fields dataclass keeps every consumer\non one code path:\n\n* ``has_raw=True``  → :data:`accel_xyz` is set; :func:`run_accel_algorithm`\n  in :mod:`python.imu_bpm_estimator` does the §6.3 autocorr work.\n* ``has_freq=True`` → :data:`frequency_hz` is set; the estimator skips\n  straight to :func:`python.imu.freq_to_bpm.freq_to_bpm`.\n* Both: caller picks per §6.10.5 (default = freq, fallback = raw).\n\nThat contract — capability bits *and* the field they unlock both have to\nbe set — is what the constructor and :meth:`__post_init__` enforce so\nbuggy upstream code fails loudly instead of silently feeding zeros to\nthe BPM estimator.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n__all__ = [\"IMUSample\", \"FrequencyUnit\"]\n\nFrequencyUnit = str\n\"\"\"``\"hz\"`` (cycles per second), ``\"rpm\"``, or ``\"bpm\"``.\n\nKept as a plain str alias instead of an Enum so JSON / OSC payloads stay\ntrivially round-trippable. :func:`python.imu.freq_to_bpm.freq_to_bpm`\ndoes the case-insensitive validation.\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass IMUSample:\n    \"\"\"One atomic telemetry frame from any IMU source.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    timestamp : float\n        Monotonic seconds. Producers MUST use a single clock per source\n        (typically :func:`time.monotonic`); the BPM estimator treats\n        ``t`` as strictly increasing within a source and will skip a\n        sample whose ``timestamp`` rewinds.\n    source_id : str\n        Stable identifier for the originating device, e.g. ``\"wrist_L_imu1\"``\n        or ``\"phone_alice\"``. Used by the estimator to keep per-source\n        rolling buffers and One-Euro state separate.\n    confidence : float, default 1.0\n        Producer-supplied trust score in ``[0, 1]``. Hardware DSP that\n        gives ``frequency_hz`` should populate this; raw-only adapters\n        usually leave it at 1.0 and let the estimator score downstream.\n    accel_xyz : tuple[float, float, float] or None\n        m/s² in the device's body frame. Set together with\n        ``has_raw=True``.\n    gyro_xyz : tuple[float, float, float] or None\n        rad/s. Reserved for future drift correction; not consumed by the\n        P1/P2 BPM estimator.\n    frequency_hz : float or None\n        Cyclic motion frequency reported by on-device DSP (mode B).\n        Always **non-negative** when set. Combine with\n        ``frequency_unit`` to disambiguate hz / rpm / bpm — the field\n        name is \"hz\" because that's the most common reporting; the\n        unit string overrides.\n    frequency_unit : str, default ``\"hz\"``\n        Either ``\"hz\"``, ``\"rpm\"``, or ``\"bpm\"``.\n    phase_pct : float or None\n        Optional 0..1 phase tag from hardware that exposes it (so the\n        estimator can skip the phase-from-autocorr step). Wraps mod 1.0.\n    has_raw, has_freq : bool\n        Capability flags. The constructor will auto-set them when their\n        respective fields are populated, but callers can override (e.g.\n        a frequency-only device that *also* attaches a single accel\n        sample for diagnostics may want ``has_raw=False`` so the\n        estimator does not start the heavy autocorr path).\n\n    Examples\n    --------\n    Pure raw (mode A — phone, ESP32 raw, P2 PhoneWSAdapter)::\n\n        IMUSample(timestamp=t, source_id=\"phone_alice\",\n                  accel_xyz=(0.1, 9.7, 0.3), has_raw=True)\n\n    Pure frequency (mode B — ESP32 with on-MCU Goertzel, AppleWatch)::\n\n        IMUSample(timestamp=t, source_id=\"wrist_L_imu1\",\n                  frequency_hz=2.0, has_freq=True, confidence=0.92)\n\n    Both (mode C — devices that report both for ground-truthing)::\n\n        IMUSample(timestamp=t, source_id=\"wrist_L_imu1\",\n                  accel_xyz=(0.0, 9.81, 0.0),\n                  frequency_hz=2.0,\n                  has_raw=True, has_freq=True)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    timestamp: float\n    source_id: str\n    confidence: float = 1.0\n\n    # --- Mode A / C: raw signal ---\n    accel_xyz: Optional[tuple[float, float, float]] = None\n    gyro_xyz: Optional[tuple[float, float, float]] = None\n\n    # --- Mode B / C: hardware-preprocessed signal ---\n    frequency_hz: Optional[float] = None\n    frequency_unit: FrequencyUnit = \"hz\"\n    phase_pct: Optional[float] = None\n\n    # --- Capability bits (auto-derived if left default) ---\n    has_raw: bool = False\n    has_freq: bool = False\n\n    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n    \"\"\"Producer-specific metadata (battery, device_kind, RSSI, …).\n    The estimator never inspects this; it's a sidecar for OSC bridge /\n    HUD layers that want richer diagnostics without bloating the schema.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if not isinstance(self.source_id, str) or not self.source_id:\n            raise ValueError(\"IMUSample.source_id must be a non-empty string\")\n        try:\n            t = float(self.timestamp)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n            raise ValueError(\"IMUSample.timestamp must be a float\") from exc\n        self.timestamp = t\n\n        # Auto-derive capability bits when the caller didn't override them.\n        # We *only* infer \"True\" — never silently flip a True flag back to\n        # False, so producers that intentionally lie about a frequency\n        # reading (diagnostic-only) keep their override.\n        if self.accel_xyz is not None and not self.has_raw:\n            self.has_raw = True\n        if self.frequency_hz is not None and not self.has_freq:\n            self.has_freq = True\n\n        # Sanity-check populated fields without forcing presence; an\n        # IMUSource may emit a heartbeat with neither (the estimator\n        # treats that as \"no reading this tick\").\n        if self.accel_xyz is not None and len(self.accel_xyz) != 3:\n            raise ValueError(\"accel_xyz must be a 3-tuple (m/s²)\")\n        if self.gyro_xyz is not None and len(self.gyro_xyz) != 3:\n            raise ValueError(\"gyro_xyz must be a 3-tuple (rad/s)\")\n\n        if self.frequency_hz is not None:\n            if self.frequency_hz < 0.0:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"frequency_hz must be >= 0; got {self.frequency_hz}\"\n                )\n            unit = str(self.frequency_unit).lower()\n            if unit not in (\"hz\", \"rpm\", \"bpm\"):\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"frequency_unit must be one of hz/rpm/bpm; got \"\n                    f\"{self.frequency_unit!r}\"\n                )\n            self.frequency_unit = unit\n\n        if self.phase_pct is not None:\n            self.phase_pct = float(self.phase_pct) % 1.0\n\n        c = float(self.confidence)\n        if c < 0.0:\n            c = 0.0\n        elif c > 1.0:\n            c = 1.0\n        self.confidence = c\n\n    def has_any_reading(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when the sample carries either raw or freq data.\n\n        Used by :class:`python.imu_bpm_estimator.DualPathEstimator` to\n        decide between \"advance the rolling buffer\" and \"no-op tick\"\n        without poking at the optional fields directly.\n        \"\"\"\n        return self.has_raw or self.has_freq\n"
```

```json
{
 "path": "D:\\文档\\Cursor\\musician gym\\python\\imu\\source.py",
 "contents": "\"\"\"\nSPEC §6.10.2 ``IMUSource`` Protocol.\n\nEvery IMU adapter — :class:`python.imu.fake.FakeAdapter`,\n``PhoneWSAdapter`` (P2), ``ESP32WiFiAdapter`` (P4),\n:class:`python.imu.osc_bridge.OSCImuBridgeAdapter` — implements the\ncontract below. The BPM estimator and :class:`LaneController` only see\nthis Protocol, never the concrete class, so the rest of the project is\nhardware-agnostic.\n\nCapabilities\n------------\n``capabilities()`` returns a frozenset whose elements are one of:\n\n* ``\"accel\"`` — produces ``accel_xyz`` samples (mode A / C in §6.10).\n* ``\"gyro\"``  — also fills ``gyro_xyz``. ``\"gyro\"`` always implies ``\"accel\"``;\n  the latter is the only signal the BPM estimator currently consumes.\n* ``\"freq\"``  — produces ``frequency_hz`` samples (mode B / C).\n* ``\"phase\"`` — also fills ``phase_pct``.\n\nMode-A devices return ``{\"accel\"}``; mode-B return ``{\"freq\"}``; mode-C\nreturn both. The estimator switches paths per §6.10.5 by inspecting the\n**sample's** ``has_raw / has_freq`` rather than the source-level\ncapability set, because some devices flip mode mid-stream (e.g. ESP32\nthat drops to raw when its on-chip detector is unsure). Sources should\nkeep capabilities() conservative: if you sometimes emit freq, list it.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Iterator, Protocol, runtime_checkable\n\nfrom python.imu.sample import IMUSample\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"IMUSource\",\n    \"CAPABILITY_ACCEL\",\n    \"CAPABILITY_GYRO\",\n    \"CAPABILITY_FREQ\",\n    \"CAPABILITY_PHASE\",\n    \"ALL_CAPABILITIES\",\n]\n\nCAPABILITY_ACCEL = \"accel\"\nCAPABILITY_GYRO = \"gyro\"\nCAPABILITY_FREQ = \"freq\"\nCAPABILITY_PHASE = \"phase\"\nALL_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(\n    {CAPABILITY_ACCEL, CAPABILITY_GYRO, CAPABILITY_FREQ, CAPABILITY_PHASE}\n)\n\n\n@runtime_checkable\nclass IMUSource(Protocol):\n    \"\"\"Stream-style adapter for any IMU device.\n\n    Lifecycle: ``open() → stream() → close()``. Implementations should\n    be re-entrant safe to ``close()`` (idempotent), but ``open()`` may\n    fail if called twice — adapters are expected to be one-shot.\n\n    Threading\n    ---------\n    ``stream()`` is allowed to block. Callers (orchestrator) typically\n    drive each source from its own thread or asyncio task, then fan-in\n    the samples. The Protocol does **not** mandate thread-safety on the\n    adapter object itself; only the ``stream()`` iteration must be safe\n    for the single consumer thread that owns it.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    source_id: str\n    \"\"\"Stable id used as :attr:`IMUSample.source_id`.\"\"\"\n\n    def capabilities(self) -> frozenset[str]:\n        \"\"\"Return a subset of :data:`ALL_CAPABILITIES`. Never empty.\"\"\"\n\n    def open(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Acquire hardware / network resources. May raise on connect failure.\"\"\"\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Release resources. Must be idempotent.\"\"\"\n\n    def stream(self) -> Iterator[IMUSample]:\n        \"\"\"Yield samples until the source is closed or exhausted.\n\n        Implementations SHOULD raise :class:`StopIteration` (or simply\n        return) when ``close()`` has been called rather than blocking\n        forever; the orchestrator joins the producer thread on shutdown.\n        \"\"\"\n"
}
```

```json
 "contents": "\"\"\"\nSPEC §6.10.3 P1 — :class:`FakeAdapter`.\n\nDrives the :class:`python.imu.IMUSource` protocol with synthetic\nsamples so the audio chain (BPM estimator → Lane Controller → OSC →\nPure Data) can be exercised end-to-end **without any hardware** during\nP1 listening tests and CI smoke checks.\n\nTwo output modes\n----------------\n* ``mode=\"freq\"`` (default — the §6.10.3 P1 row): emits a constant\n  ``frequency_hz`` so the dual-path estimator (:mod:`python.imu_bpm_estimator`)\n  takes its fast path through :func:`python.imu.freq_to_bpm.freq_to_bpm`.\n* ``mode=\"accel\"``: synthesises a sinusoidal vertical acceleration at\n  ``frequency_hz`` so the slow autocorr path in :mod:`python.bpm.accel_autocorr`\n  has realistic input. Useful for proving the §6.3 algorithm on\n  hardware-free CI.\n\nBoth modes can be combined (``mode=\"both\"``, the §6.10.1 *mode C*\nrow) so a unit test can verify the estimator's fast/slow arbitration.\n\nDesign notes\n------------\n- **Pull-based ``stream()``**: yields one sample every ``interval_s``\n  seconds. Backed by a :class:`threading.Event` so :meth:`close` wakes\n  any blocking consumer immediately. The timing policy is intentionally\n  simple — no precise drift compensation — because real adapters ship\n  *their* timestamps; the smoothing happens downstream.\n- **Injectable clock + sleep**: tests pass ``clock=`` and ``sleep=``\n  callables to drive the stream deterministically without real wall-clock\n  delay. Production callers leave the defaults to use :func:`time.monotonic`.\n- **Optional jitter**: ``frequency_jitter_hz`` adds Gaussian noise to\n  each emitted ``frequency_hz`` (mode B/C); ``accel_noise_g`` does the\n  same for the synthesised accel signal (mode A/C). Both default to 0.0\n  so deterministic tests stay deterministic.\n- **No dependency on numpy / scipy** at the top level: the file imports\n  numpy lazily *inside* the accel path, so a CI worker that only needs\n  the freq path (FastAdapter on a stripped-down image) can run without\n  scipy/numpy in scope.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport random\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Callable, Iterator, Literal, Optional\n\nfrom python.imu.sample import IMUSample\nfrom python.imu.source import (\n    CAPABILITY_ACCEL,\n    CAPABILITY_FREQ,\n    CAPABILITY_PHASE,\n    IMUSource,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\"FakeAdapter\", \"FakeMode\"]\n\nFakeMode = Literal[\"freq\", \"accel\", \"both\"]\n\"\"\"Output flavour. See module docstring.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _default_sleep(seconds: float) -> None:\n    if seconds > 0.0:\n        time.sleep(seconds)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass FakeAdapter:\n    \"\"\"Hardware-free :class:`IMUSource` for P1 / CI.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    source_id : str, default ``\"fake_imu\"``\n        Tag used as :attr:`IMUSample.source_id`. Tests with multiple\n        adapters should make this unique so the estimator keeps per-source\n        state separate.\n    frequency_hz : float, default 2.0\n        Base motion frequency. ``2.0 Hz`` ≈ a 120 BPM squat under the\n        §6.10.4 ``(\"esp32_wrist\", \"squat\") -> 60`` mapping, so the\n        default already lands in the listenable lane range.\n    mode : ``\"freq\" | \"accel\" | \"both\"``, default ``\"freq\"``\n        Which sample fields to populate. See module docstring.\n    interval_s : float, default 0.02\n        Period between emitted samples. ``0.02`` matches a ~50 Hz feed,\n        comparable to a phone DeviceMotion event rate. Set to ``0.0`` to\n        emit as fast as the consumer pulls (mostly for unit tests).\n    confidence : float, default 1.0\n        Constant confidence stamped on every sample. Useful for\n        modelling \"signal lost\" via 0.0 in tests.\n    frequency_jitter_hz : float, default 0.0\n        Gaussian σ added to ``frequency_hz`` per sample. Modelled in\n        Hz, not BPM, because that's the unit the §6.10.5 fast path\n        consumes; pre-mapping noise gives the most faithful smoke test.\n    accel_noise_g : float, default 0.0\n        Gaussian σ added to each accel axis (in g, multiplied by\n        ``9.81`` internally). 0.05 is roughly the noise floor of an\n        MPU-6050; 0.5 stress-tests the autocorr path's narrowband filter.\n    accel_amp_g : float, default 0.6\n        Half-amplitude of the synthesised vertical accel sinusoid (in g).\n        0.6 g matches a vigorous squat / jumping jack as measured on a\n        wrist-band; 0.2 g is a casual motion. Combined with gravity\n        (9.81 m/s² along ``+y``) so the autocorr path sees realistic\n        ``|a|`` modulation.\n    phase_pct : float or None, default ``None``\n        Optional fixed phase fraction. ``None`` lets the adapter compute\n        a freely-running phase from ``timestamp`` and ``frequency_hz``.\n    seed : int or None, default ``None``\n        Seeds the internal :class:`random.Random` for reproducible\n        jitter. ``None`` follows :class:`random.Random()`'s OS seed.\n    clock : callable, default :func:`time.monotonic`\n        Returns monotonic seconds. Tests inject a mutable clock to\n        deterministically advance time.\n    sleep : callable, default :func:`time.sleep`\n        Pause function (signature ``sleep(seconds)``). Tests pass a\n        no-op lambda so ``stream()`` returns instantly per tick.\n\n    Examples\n    --------\n    Pure freq, deterministic for unit tests::\n\n        adapter = FakeAdapter(\n            frequency_hz=2.0, mode=\"freq\",\n            sleep=lambda _s: None, interval_s=0.0,\n        )\n        adapter.open()\n        samples = list(zip(range(5), adapter.stream()))\n        adapter.close()\n\n    Live freq + accel for the dual-path estimator::\n\n        adapter = FakeAdapter(frequency_hz=1.5, mode=\"both\", source_id=\"dev1\")\n        with adapter:\n            for sample in adapter.stream():\n                bpm, phase, conf = estimator.update(sample)\n                ...\n    \"\"\"\n\n    source_id: str = \"fake_imu\"\n    frequency_hz: float = 2.0\n    mode: FakeMode = \"freq\"\n    interval_s: float = 0.02\n    confidence: float = 1.0\n    frequency_jitter_hz: float = 0.0\n    accel_noise_g: float = 0.0\n    accel_amp_g: float = 0.6\n    phase_pct: Optional[float] = None\n    seed: Optional[int] = None\n    clock: Callable[[], float] = field(default=time.monotonic)\n    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = field(default=_default_sleep)\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.frequency_hz < 0.0:\n            raise ValueError(\"frequency_hz must be >= 0\")\n        if self.interval_s < 0.0:\n            raise ValueError(\"interval_s must be >= 0\")\n        if self.mode not in (\"freq\", \"accel\", \"both\"):\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"mode must be 'freq' | 'accel' | 'both'; got {self.mode!r}\"\n            )\n        if self.accel_amp_g < 0.0:\n            raise ValueError(\"accel_amp_g must be >= 0\")\n        # Confidence is forced into [0, 1] downstream; surface a friendly\n        # error here so a typo (`confidence=10`) doesn't silently clamp.\n        if not (0.0 <= float(self.confidence) <= 1.0):\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"confidence must lie in [0, 1]; got {self.confidence}\"\n            )\n        self._opened = False\n        self._stop = threading.Event()\n        self._t0: Optional[float] = None\n        self._rng = random.Random(self.seed)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # IMUSource Protocol\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def capabilities(self) -> frozenset[str]:\n        caps: set[str] = set()\n        if self.mode in (\"freq\", \"both\"):\n            caps.add(CAPABILITY_FREQ)\n            caps.add(CAPABILITY_PHASE)\n        if self.mode in (\"accel\", \"both\"):\n            caps.add(CAPABILITY_ACCEL)\n        return frozenset(caps)\n\n    def open(self) -> None:\n        if self._opened:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"FakeAdapter is already open; instantiate a new one\")\n        self._opened = True\n        self._stop.clear()\n        self._t0 = self.clock()\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        # Idempotent: caller can repeat in a finally / __exit__ without\n        # blowing up if open() never ran.\n        self._stop.set()\n        self._opened = False\n\n    def stream(self) -> Iterator[IMUSample]:\n        if not self._opened:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"FakeAdapter.stream() called before open()\")\n        while not self._stop.is_set():\n            yield self._make_sample()\n            if self.interval_s > 0.0:\n                self.sleep(self.interval_s)\n            else:\n                # Yield CPU politely even with interval=0; protects the\n                # rare test that runs adapter+consumer in one thread and\n                # expects fairness without changing semantics.\n                self.sleep(0.0)\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> \"FakeAdapter\":\n        self.open()\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Internals\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def _make_sample(self) -> IMUSample:\n        now = self.clock()\n        elapsed = now - (self._t0 if self._t0 is not None else now)\n\n        freq = max(0.0, self._jittered_freq())\n        phase = self._phase_for(elapsed, freq)\n\n        accel_xyz: Optional[tuple[float, float, float]] = None\n        if self.mode in (\"accel\", \"both\"):\n            accel_xyz = self._synthesise_accel(elapsed, freq)\n\n        # Only fill freq fields in modes that advertise it. We always\n        # supply phase when it's available so consumers can skip the\n        # phase-from-autocorr step when they trust the source.\n        frequency_hz: Optional[float] = freq if self.mode in (\"freq\", \"both\") else None\n        phase_pct: Optional[float] = (\n            (self.phase_pct if self.phase_pct is not None else phase)\n            if self.mode in (\"freq\", \"both\")\n            else None\n        )\n\n        return IMUSample(\n            timestamp=now,\n            source_id=self.source_id,\n            confidence=self.confidence,\n            accel_xyz=accel_xyz,\n            frequency_hz=frequency_hz,\n            phase_pct=phase_pct,\n        )\n\n    def _jittered_freq(self) -> float:\n        if self.frequency_jitter_hz <= 0.0:\n            return self.frequency_hz\n        return self.frequency_hz + self._rng.gauss(0.0, self.frequency_jitter_hz)\n\n    def _phase_for(self, elapsed: float, freq: float) -> float:\n        if freq <= 0.0:\n            return 0.0\n        return (elapsed * freq) % 1.0\n\n    def _synthesise_accel(\n        self, elapsed: float, freq: float\n    ) -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n        # Gravity sits on +y so |a| ≈ 9.81 at rest, then modulates with\n        # the simulated motion — the same shape the §6.3 autocorr expects.\n        g = 9.81\n        amp = self.accel_amp_g * g\n        omega = 2.0 * math.pi * max(0.0, freq)\n        ay = g + amp * math.sin(omega * elapsed)\n        ax = 0.0\n        az = 0.0\n        if self.accel_noise_g > 0.0:\n            sigma = self.accel_noise_g * g\n            ax += self._rng.gauss(0.0, sigma)\n            ay += self._rng.gauss(0.0, sigma)\n            az += self._rng.gauss(0.0, sigma)\n        return (ax, ay, az)\n\n\n# Sanity assertion at import-time: FakeAdapter must satisfy IMUSource.\n# A bare Protocol can't be instantiated, so we just ensure structural\n# compatibility — getting this wrong would only show up at runtime\n# inside :class:`DualPathEstimator`, far from the cause.\nassert isinstance(FakeAdapter(source_id=\"self_check\"), IMUSource), (  # noqa: S101\n    \"FakeAdapter no longer implements IMUSource; check protocol drift.\"\n)\n"
}
```

## UPDATE A2 + PICK A3 — `python/imu/freq_to_bpm.py`

 A2 passed all three mode configurations correctly — freq-only has the right capabilities and flags, both mode includes everything, and accel-only properly excludes frequency data. Now I'm moving on to A3, which involves the frequency-to-BPM conversion module in the Python IMU code.

I'm designing a mapping table and conversion function following the spec: a BPM_FROM_FREQ dictionary that maps device and action pairs to conversion coefficients, with a freq_to_bpm() function that branches based on the sample's frequency unit and falls back gracefully from specific device-action combinations to device-only defaults to a hardcoded 60.0 constant. I'm also building in a register() function for runtime calibration and making sure the fallback logic is clearly exposed.

```json
 "path": "D:\\文档\\Cursor\\musician gym\\python\\imu\\freq_to_bpm.py",
 "contents": "\"\"\"\nSPEC §6.10.4 — frequency → BPM mapping.\n\nHardware-reported \"motion frequency\" cannot be naively multiplied by\n60: each ``(device_kind, action_id)`` pair has a different cycle\ndefinition. The classic example from §6.10.4:\n\n    A wrist-worn IMU calls one squat (down-up) \"1 cycle\";\n    an ankle-worn IMU watching ``high_knees`` may double-count because\n    it sees both legs cross the gate per rep.\n\nSo we keep an explicit lookup table and let the calibration flow at\nthe end of §6.10.4 (30 s of paced movement) write back the right ``k``\nat session start.\n\nAPI surface\n-----------\n\n* :data:`BPM_FROM_FREQ` — mutable dict, default-populated with the SPEC\n  rows. Calibration code may overwrite or insert new entries; the\n  package keeps a fallback ``(*, \"*\") -> 60.0`` baked-in via\n  :func:`freq_to_bpm` so unknown combinations stay listenable instead\n  of going to 0.\n* :func:`freq_to_bpm` — convert one :class:`IMUSample` (or raw\n  ``frequency_hz``) into a BPM number.\n* :func:`register_mapping` / :func:`reset_mappings_to_default` — small\n  helpers around the dict so the calibration tool doesn't need to\n  reach into module state directly.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Optional, Tuple\n\nfrom python.imu.sample import IMUSample\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"BPM_FROM_FREQ\",\n    \"DEFAULT_BPM_FROM_FREQ\",\n    \"DEVICE_KIND_WILDCARD\",\n    \"ACTION_ID_WILDCARD\",\n    \"DEFAULT_K\",\n    \"freq_to_bpm\",\n    \"register_mapping\",\n    \"reset_mappings_to_default\",\n]\n\nDEVICE_KIND_WILDCARD: str = \"*\"\n\"\"\"Used as a key in :data:`BPM_FROM_FREQ` for \"any device of this kind\"\nor, paired with action ``\"*\"``, the universal fallback.\"\"\"\n\nACTION_ID_WILDCARD: str = \"*\"\n\"\"\"Used as a key in :data:`BPM_FROM_FREQ` for \"any action of this device\".\"\"\"\n\nDEFAULT_K: float = 60.0\n\"\"\"Last-resort multiplier when neither ``(device, action)`` nor\n``(device, \"*\")`` is registered. ``60.0`` matches \"1 Hz = 60 BPM\"\nwhich is the safe assumption for any well-behaved wrist or ankle IMU\nrunning at 1 cycle / rep — far better than dropping the lane to 0.\"\"\"\n\nDEFAULT_BPM_FROM_FREQ: dict[Tuple[str, str], float] = {\n    # SPEC §6.10.4 reference table. The pairs that are explicit here\n    # are the ones we already know diverge from the simple \"1 Hz = 60 BPM\"\n    # heuristic; everything else falls through DEFAULT_K.\n    (\"esp32_wrist\", \"squat\"): 60.0,\n    (\"esp32_wrist\", \"jumping_jack\"): 60.0,\n    (\"esp32_wrist\", \"punch\"): 60.0,\n    (\"esp32_ankle\", \"high_knees\"): 30.0,\n    (\"esp32_ankle\", \"squat\"): 60.0,\n    (\"apple_watch\", \"squat\"): 60.0,\n    (\"apple_watch\", \"jumping_jack\"): 60.0,\n    (\"apple_watch\", \"punch\"): 60.0,\n    (\"mi_band\", ACTION_ID_WILDCARD): 60.0,\n    # Phone-as-IMU comes from DeviceMotion at 50–60 Hz. We assume the\n    # accel autocorr path picks the right peak so frequency reaches us\n    # already in \"rep/s\" — same multiplier as a wristband.\n    (\"phone\", ACTION_ID_WILDCARD): 60.0,\n    # Unit tests + the FakeAdapter intentionally use a stable default,\n    # so leaving 60 means the P1 listening test \"fake -> Pd\" stays in\n    # the listenable lane range without touching the table.\n    (\"fake_imu\", ACTION_ID_WILDCARD): 60.0,\n}\n\"\"\"Authoritative defaults. :data:`BPM_FROM_FREQ` is initialised from\nthis and may be hot-edited by calibration; call\n:func:`reset_mappings_to_default` to restore.\"\"\"\n\nBPM_FROM_FREQ: dict[Tuple[str, str], float] = dict(DEFAULT_BPM_FROM_FREQ)\n\"\"\"Live mapping table. Imported by :func:`freq_to_bpm`. Mutating it\n*persists* for the duration of the process — tests that need isolation\nshould call :func:`reset_mappings_to_default` in teardown.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef register_mapping(device_kind: str, action_id: str, k: float) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Insert / replace a calibration entry.\n\n    Wraps the dict assignment so calibration tooling has a single\n    breakpoint-friendly line to debug. Validates the inputs because\n    a typo'd ``k`` (e.g. ``60`` written as ``\"60\"``) would silently\n    bork every later lookup.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(device_kind, str) or not device_kind:\n        raise ValueError(\"device_kind must be a non-empty string\")\n    if not isinstance(action_id, str) or not action_id:\n        raise ValueError(\"action_id must be a non-empty string\")\n    k_f = float(k)\n    if k_f <= 0.0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"k must be > 0; got {k}\")\n    BPM_FROM_FREQ[(device_kind, action_id)] = k_f\n\n\ndef reset_mappings_to_default() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Restore :data:`BPM_FROM_FREQ` to :data:`DEFAULT_BPM_FROM_FREQ`.\"\"\"\n    BPM_FROM_FREQ.clear()\n    BPM_FROM_FREQ.update(DEFAULT_BPM_FROM_FREQ)\n\n\ndef _lookup_k(device_kind: str, action_id: str) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Three-tier lookup: exact → device wildcard → universal default.\"\"\"\n    k = BPM_FROM_FREQ.get((device_kind, action_id))\n    if k is not None:\n        return k\n    k = BPM_FROM_FREQ.get((device_kind, ACTION_ID_WILDCARD))\n    if k is not None:\n        return k\n    k = BPM_FROM_FREQ.get(\n        (DEVICE_KIND_WILDCARD, ACTION_ID_WILDCARD)\n    )\n    if k is not None:\n        return k\n    return DEFAULT_K\n\n\ndef freq_to_bpm(\n    sample_or_freq: IMUSample | float | None,\n    action_id: str = ACTION_ID_WILDCARD,\n    device_kind: str = DEVICE_KIND_WILDCARD,\n    *,\n    unit: Optional[str] = None,\n) -> Optional[float]:\n    \"\"\"Convert a hardware-reported frequency to BPM (§6.10.4).\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    sample_or_freq : IMUSample | float | None\n        Either a full sample (preferred — the unit + value are taken\n        from the sample) or a bare ``frequency_hz``. ``None`` returns\n        ``None`` to keep \"no reading this tick\" plumbing trivial.\n    action_id : str\n        Lookup key. Pass the **detected** action so the table maps\n        the right cycle definition (the §6.2.7 / §6.10.6 coupling).\n        Use ``\"*\"`` for \"any action\" (e.g. before vision has locked on).\n    device_kind : str\n        Lookup key. Match the device's reported ``device_kind`` field\n        (``esp32_wrist`` / ``apple_watch`` / ``phone`` / ...).\n    unit : ``\"hz\" | \"rpm\" | \"bpm\"``, optional\n        Override the sample's :attr:`IMUSample.frequency_unit`. Useful\n        when ``sample_or_freq`` is a bare float and you know what unit\n        the producer used.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    float or None\n        BPM, or ``None`` when no usable frequency is available\n        (sample missing, ``frequency_hz`` ``None``, ``has_freq`` False).\n\n    Notes\n    -----\n    SPEC §6.10.4 short-circuits the table when the producer already\n    reports BPM or RPM — those units are unambiguous so the multiplier\n    table doesn't apply. Hz is the only unit that needs the lookup.\n    \"\"\"\n    freq, resolved_unit, action_for_lookup = _coerce(\n        sample_or_freq, action_id, unit\n    )\n    if freq is None:\n        return None\n\n    if resolved_unit == \"bpm\":\n        return float(freq)\n    if resolved_unit == \"rpm\":\n        # 1 RPM == 1 cycle/min == 1 rep/min == 1 BPM. Treated identically\n        # because callers pick the unit that matches their cycle definition.\n        return float(freq)\n\n    # resolved_unit == \"hz\" — the path that needs the table.\n    k = _lookup_k(device_kind, action_for_lookup)\n    return float(freq) * k\n\n\ndef _coerce(\n    sample_or_freq: IMUSample | float | None,\n    action_id: str,\n    explicit_unit: Optional[str],\n) -> Tuple[Optional[float], str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Pull (frequency, unit, action) out of either input flavour.\n\n    Centralised so the public function can stay flat. Returns ``(None, ...)``\n    when the input has no usable frequency, which short-circuits the\n    table lookup in :func:`freq_to_bpm`.\n    \"\"\"\n    if sample_or_freq is None:\n        return None, \"hz\", action_id\n\n    if isinstance(sample_or_freq, IMUSample):\n        sample = sample_or_freq\n        if not sample.has_freq or sample.frequency_hz is None:\n            return None, \"hz\", action_id\n        unit = explicit_unit or sample.frequency_unit\n        return float(sample.frequency_hz), unit.lower(), action_id\n\n    # Bare float / int path. Anything that float()s; explicitly forbid\n    # bools to avoid bool-as-int confusion (Python lets ``float(True)`` work).\n    if isinstance(sample_or_freq, bool):\n        raise TypeError(\"freq_to_bpm does not accept bool\")\n    try:\n        freq = float(sample_or_freq)\n    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n        raise TypeError(\n            f\"freq_to_bpm expected IMUSample | float | None; got \"\n            f\"{type(sample_or_freq).__name__}\"\n        ) from exc\n    unit = (explicit_unit or \"hz\").lower()\n    if unit not in (\"hz\", \"rpm\", \"bpm\"):\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"unit must be hz/rpm/bpm; got {explicit_unit!r}\"\n        )\n    return freq, unit, action_id\n"
}
```

```json
 "contents": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSPEC §9 — Fake multi-lane OSC sender for the P1 listening test.\n\nDrives Pure Data (or :mod:`tools.osc_dump`) with two parallel lanes\nplus a master kick at fixed BPMs so the listener can audition the\npolyrhythm + auto-detune path without any vision/IMU hardware.\n\nUsage::\n\n    # 听感 1 — three stems all at 120 BPM, perfectly locked\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 120 --bpm2 120 --master 120\n\n    # 听感 2 — lane2 drags 90 BPM (slow) against 120 master\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 120 --bpm2 90  --master 120\n\n    # 听感 3 — lane1 rushes 150 BPM\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 150 --bpm2 120 --master 120\n\n    # 听感 4 — full polyrhythm\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 150 --bpm2 90  --master 120\n\n    # 验证 heartbeat-保险：3s 后 Pd 应自动静音\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 120 --duration 5\n\n    # 模拟 climb：master 在 30s 内从 90 渐进到 150\n    python tools/fake_multi_lane_sender.py --bpm1 120 --bpm2 110 \\\n        --master 90 --master-end 150 --duration 30\n\nThe script reuses :class:`python.osc.LaneOscSender` so the OSC namespace\nstays in lock-step with SPEC §6.5; if the namespace ever changes, this\ntool follows automatically without edits.\n\nStage-A specific behaviour\n--------------------------\n- Sends ``/mg/lane/{i}/bpm`` and ``/mg/lane/{i}/delta_bpm`` (delta vs\n  current master) so Pure Data can drive its detune side-chain without\n  recomputing the math.\n- Sends ``/mg/lane/{i}/gain`` = 1.0 (no penalty in P1; the §6.4 decay\n  belongs to the live :class:`LaneController`).\n- Sends ``/mg/master/bpm`` once per tick.\n- Sends ``/mg/sys/heartbeat`` once per tick at the same rate so Pd's\n  3-second silence guard sees a steady pulse.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport math\nimport signal\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterable, List, Optional\n\n_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nif str(_ROOT) not in sys.path:\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(_ROOT))\n\nfrom python.osc import LaneOscSender\n\n\ndef _parse_bpm_list(spec: str) -> List[float]:\n    \"\"\"Comma-separated BPMs ``\"120,100,140\"`` → ``[120.0, 100.0, 140.0]``.\"\"\"\n    out: list[float] = []\n    for tok in spec.split(\",\"):\n        tok = tok.strip()\n        if not tok:\n            continue\n        out.append(float(tok))\n    if not out:\n        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(\"expected at least one BPM value\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef parse_args(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> argparse.Namespace:\n    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"fake_multi_lane_sender\",\n        description=(\n            \"SPEC §9 P1 — drive Pd with synthetic per-lane BPMs, \"\n            \"no camera/IMU required.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\"--bpm1\", type=float, default=120.0, help=\"Lane 1 BPM (default 120)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--bpm2\", type=float, default=100.0, help=\"Lane 2 BPM (default 100)\")\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--bpm\",\n        type=_parse_bpm_list,\n        default=None,\n        help=(\n            \"Comma-separated BPMs to override --bpm1/--bpm2 and unlock more \"\n            \"lanes (e.g. '120,100,140,80'). Lane indices are 1-based.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\"--master\", type=float, default=120.0, help=\"Master BPM (default 120)\")\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--master-end\",\n        type=float,\n        default=None,\n        help=(\n            \"Optional climb target. When set, master BPM linearly slews from \"\n            \"--master to --master-end over --duration seconds.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\"--host\", default=\"***REDACTED-IP***\", help=\"OSC host (default ***REDACTED-IP***)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=5005, help=\"OSC port (default 5005)\")\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--rate\",\n        type=float,\n        default=10.0,\n        help=(\n            \"Send rate in Hz (default 10). Pd's heartbeat guard expects ≥ 1 Hz; \"\n            \"10 Hz keeps the whole pipeline responsive without flooding.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--duration\",\n        type=float,\n        default=0.0,\n        help=(\n            \"Stop after this many seconds (default 0 = run until Ctrl-C). \"\n            \"Combined with --master-end this also defines the climb length.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--quiet\",\n        action=\"store_true\",\n        help=\"Suppress per-second status prints.\",\n    )\n    return p.parse_args(argv)\n\n\ndef _resolve_lane_bpms(args: argparse.Namespace) -> List[float]:\n    \"\"\"Decide the per-lane BPM list.\n\n    ``--bpm`` (CSV) wins when given; otherwise we fall back to the\n    default ``--bpm1 / --bpm2`` pair so the SPEC §9 listening recipes\n    keep working unchanged.\n    \"\"\"\n    if args.bpm is not None:\n        return list(args.bpm)\n    return [float(args.bpm1), float(args.bpm2)]\n\n\ndef _master_at(t: float, base: float, end: Optional[float], total: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Linear climb if ``end`` is set, else constant ``base``.\n\n    Returns ``end`` once ``t >= total`` so a climb that runs longer than\n    the configured duration doesn't drift past the target — the SPEC §3\n    auto-climb requirement explicitly hits the goal value cleanly.\n    \"\"\"\n    if end is None or total <= 0.0:\n        return base\n    if t >= total:\n        return float(end)\n    frac = max(0.0, t / total)\n    return base + (end - base) * frac\n\n\ndef _build_senders(\n    *, host: str, port: int, n_lanes: int\n) -> List[LaneOscSender]:\n    return [\n        LaneOscSender(host=host, port=port, lane_id=i + 1)\n        for i in range(n_lanes)\n    ]\n\n\ndef main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:\n    args = parse_args(argv)\n    lane_bpms = _resolve_lane_bpms(args)\n    senders = _build_senders(host=args.host, port=args.port, n_lanes=len(lane_bpms))\n\n    if args.rate <= 0.0:\n        print(\"error: --rate must be > 0\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n    period = 1.0 / float(args.rate)\n\n    # Graceful Ctrl-C: keep KeyboardInterrupt path intact for tests but\n    # also catch SIGTERM so Docker / systemd shutdowns don't dump a stack.\n    stop = {\"flag\": False}\n\n    def _on_signal(_signum: int, _frame: object) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - signal-driven\n        stop[\"flag\"] = True\n\n    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _on_signal)\n    if hasattr(signal, \"SIGTERM\"):\n        try:\n            signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _on_signal)\n        except (ValueError, OSError):\n            # SIGTERM isn't installable from non-main threads on Windows;\n            # the SIGINT path still fires on Ctrl-C, so skip gracefully.\n            pass\n\n    if not args.quiet:\n        bpm_str = \", \".join(f\"L{i+1}={b:.1f}\" for i, b in enumerate(lane_bpms))\n        climb = (\n            f\"  (climb master → {args.master_end:.1f} over {args.duration:.1f}s)\"\n            if args.master_end is not None and args.duration > 0\n            else \"\"\n        )\n        print(\n            f\"[fake-multi] sending OSC to {args.host}:{args.port} @ \"\n            f\"{args.rate:.1f} Hz — master={args.master:.1f}, {bpm_str}{climb}\",\n            flush=True,\n        )\n\n    t0 = time.monotonic()\n    next_status_at = t0 + 1.0\n    next_send_at = t0\n    sent_ticks = 0\n\n    try:\n        while not stop[\"flag\"]:\n            now = time.monotonic()\n            if args.duration > 0.0 and now - t0 >= args.duration:\n                break\n            if now < next_send_at:\n                time.sleep(min(0.005, next_send_at - now))\n                continue\n\n            elapsed = now - t0\n            master_bpm = _master_at(\n                elapsed, args.master, args.master_end, args.duration\n            )\n\n            # Master fans out to every lane; we only send the master line\n            # once per tick from sender 0 because all senders share a UDP\n            # socket and the address is global.\n            senders[0].send_master_bpm(master_bpm)\n            senders[0].send_heartbeat(value=int(elapsed * args.rate) % 1024)\n\n            for sender, lane_bpm in zip(senders, lane_bpms):\n                sender.send_bpm(lane_bpm)\n                sender.send_delta_bpm(lane_bpm - master_bpm)\n                # SPEC §6.5 keeps gain semantically separate from BPM so\n                # Pd patches can mix Master+lane without doing math; the\n                # P1 sender always claims gain=1.0 (no penalty in offline\n                # auditions — the live LaneController is what ramps it\n                # down on missed beats).\n                sender.send_gain(1.0)\n\n            sent_ticks += 1\n            next_send_at += period\n            # Drift recovery: if we fell behind by more than one period\n            # (because the consumer sleep ran long), snap forward instead\n            # of bursting catch-up packets that the heartbeat guard would\n            # interpret as jitter.\n            if next_send_at < now - period:\n                next_send_at = now + period\n\n            if not args.quiet and now >= next_status_at:\n                print(\n                    _status_line(\n                        elapsed=elapsed,\n                        master_bpm=master_bpm,\n                        lane_bpms=lane_bpms,\n                        sent_ticks=sent_ticks,\n                    ),\n                    flush=True,\n                )\n                next_status_at = now + 1.0\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        pass\n\n    if not args.quiet:\n        print(\n            f\"[fake-multi] done — sent {sent_ticks} ticks across \"\n            f\"{len(senders)} lanes ({time.monotonic() - t0:.2f}s)\",\n            flush=True,\n        )\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _status_line(\n    *,\n    elapsed: float,\n    master_bpm: float,\n    lane_bpms: Iterable[float],\n    sent_ticks: int,\n) -> str:\n    deltas = \", \".join(\n        f\"L{i+1}Δ={lb - master_bpm:+.1f}\"\n        for i, lb in enumerate(lane_bpms)\n    )\n    return (\n        f\"  [+{elapsed:6.2f}s] master={master_bpm:6.2f}  {deltas}  \"\n        f\"ticks={sent_ticks}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef _isfinite_positive(x: float) -> bool:\n    return math.isfinite(x) and x > 0.0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}
```

## UPDATE A4 + PICK A5 — 重写 `pd/song.pd` 多 lane grain + master kick

 A4 passed with 80 packets covering all required SPEC §6.5 P1 fields, the master tempo climbed from 120 to around 147 BPM within a second, and the heartbeat tracked changes across 10 cycles. Now I'm moving to A5, which involves rewriting the Pd patch to support multiple lane grains with a master kick element.

The current `pd/song.pd` is just an OSC printer, so I need to build out the actual audio synthesis layer. I'm designing a simplified but functional patch that receives OSC messages via netreceive, parses them, routes the lane and master control signals, then feeds them through metro-driven sample playback with gain and detune modulation before mixing to the audio output.

Since I don't have the actual stem assets yet, I'll substitute with synthesized tones instead of tabread4~ grain playback for now.

My approach is straightforward: each lane triggers a short noise or sine burst with an envelope on every beat—lane 1 gets a low bass noise, lane 2 a mid-range sine click, and the master outputs a kick drum. I'll structure each lane with a metro that fires at the calculated period in milliseconds, then route that trigger through a vline~ envelope into an oscillator before mixing everything down.

To make it easy to swap in real audio files later, I'm setting up the patch to accept OSC messages over UDP and route them to the appropriate lanes and parameters, then I'll write out the Pd patch syntax directly.

 Pure Data's file format is position-sensitive, so I need to create a patch that can play sound directly when opened in Pd. Since there are no audio stems available, I'm using synthesized tones as placeholders—each lane runs a metronome that triggers an envelope generator feeding into an oscillator, with parameters controlled by BPM, detuning, and gain values. I'm also setting up OSC routing to receive control messages over the network.

For the DSP chain, I'm calculating the oscillator frequency by taking a base frequency for each lane and applying a cents-based detune offset using the formula `base_freq * 2^(cents/1200)`. To keep the patch stable, I'm implementing a heartbeat watchdog that resets a 3-second timer whenever a heartbeat message arrives—if no heartbeat comes within that window, the master output mutes automatically.

Now I'm setting up the Pd patch structure with OSC receive, parse, and route objects, using a compact 30-pixel grid layout. I need to handle the routing carefully since `oscparse` outputs the address and arguments as a list, so I'll use nested `route` objects to split the incoming messages by their address paths.

Writing Pd patch code... 我决定直接展开完整的 selector 列表，这样虽然有 10 个 outlet 但逻辑清晰。每个 OSC 地址对应一个 outlet，然后分别处理：BPM 值转换成周期驱动 metro，detune 用来调整振荡器频率，gain 通过 line~ 平滑控制音量，master BPM 控制主节拍，heartbeat 用来重置延迟计时。每条 lane 的合成流程是 metro 触发一个短包络，乘以计算出的振荡器信号，再乘以 gain 值后输出。

## UPDATE A5 + PICK A6 — `python/imu/osc_bridge.py`

 I'm verifying the Pd patch structure—80 rows and 65 connections with no out-of-bounds references, so it should load directly in Pure Data. The patch receives OSC messages for BPM control on different lanes, triggers short envelopes synchronized to the beat, handles pitch detuning and volume adjustment, and uses a phasor-based approach for the master kick sound.

The remaining features include a heartbeat watchdog that mutes after 3 seconds of silence and a loadbang default that keeps audio unmuted so users hear output even without sending heartbeat signals. The patch uses synthesized tones as placeholder stems per the spec, but users can swap in real audio samples using tabread4~ and soundfiler if needed. The file-level validation is complete, so the next step is opening it in Pd for listening tests.

Now I'm moving to the next component: building an OSC bridge adapter for IMU data that subscribes to hardware IMU messages and converts them into IMUSample objects. The adapter will run a background OSC server listening for device-specific frequency, acceleration, battery, and binding data across multiple devices, then fuse these events together by maintaining a buffer per device ID and assembling complete samples when both frequency and acceleration signals arrive.

Writing the adapter implementation...

We therefore latch every\npiece of metadata onto a per-device buffer (:class:`_DeviceState`) and\nemit one :class:`IMUSample` whenever a *signal-bearing* address\n(``freq`` or ``accel``) arrives. The default factory builds a\n``python-osc`` ``ThreadingOSCUDPServer`` on the configured port and\nruns it in a background thread.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport queue\nimport re\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Optional\n\nfrom python.imu.sample import IMUSample\nfrom python.imu.source import (\n    ALL_CAPABILITIES,\n    CAPABILITY_ACCEL,\n    CAPABILITY_FREQ,\n    CAPABILITY_GYRO,\n    CAPABILITY_PHASE,\n    IMUSource,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"OSCImuBridgeAdapter\",\n    \"DEFAULT_BRIDGE_HOST\",\n    \"DEFAULT_BRIDGE_PORT\",\n    \"OSC_HW_PREFIX\",\n]\n\nDEFAULT_BRIDGE_HOST = \"***REDACTED-IP***\"\nDEFAULT_BRIDGE_PORT = 5006\n\"\"\"Distinct from the Pure Data receive port (5005) so a single laptop\ncan run *both* the OSC sender that drives Pd and the bridge that\nconsumes hardware-direct OSC without colliding.\"\"\"\n\nOSC_HW_PREFIX = \"/mg/hw/imu\"\n\"\"\"SPEC §6.5 ``/mg/hw/imu/{device_id}/...``. Bridge subscribes only\nto children of this; everything else is ignored so the same UDP port\ncan carry diagnostic noise without confusing the estimator.\"\"\"\n\n_ADDR_RE = re.compile(\n    rf\"^{re.escape(OSC_HW_PREFIX)}/(?P<device>[^/]+)/(?P<key>\\w+)$\"\n)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass _DeviceState:\n    \"\"\"Latched metadata for one physical device.\"\"\"\n\n    last_accel: Optional[tuple[float, float, float]] = None\n    last_gyro: Optional[tuple[float, float, float]] = None\n    last_freq_hz: Optional[float] = None\n    last_freq_conf: float = 1.0\n    last_phase: Optional[float] = None\n    device_kind: Optional[str] = None\n    battery: Optional[int] = None\n    binding: Optional[int] = None\n    last_seen: float = 0.0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass OSCImuBridgeAdapter:\n    \"\"\"Subscribe to ``/mg/hw/imu/{id}/*`` and emit :class:`IMUSample`.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    source_id : str\n        Stable identifier for the bridge as a whole. Individual sample\n        ``source_id`` fields use the per-message ``{device_id}`` so the\n        BPM estimator keeps each watch / wristband separate; the\n        bridge-level ``source_id`` is what shows up in logs and the\n        Lane Controller's source registry.\n    host, port : str / int\n        UDP address to bind. Default ``***REDACTED-IP***:5006`` matches SPEC §6.5.\n    queue_max : int, default 4096\n        Soft cap on the internal sample queue. Hitting it drops the\n        *oldest* unconsumed sample (FIFO eviction) so a slow consumer\n        never silently latches latency on a fast IMU stream.\n    server_factory : callable, optional\n        ``factory(host, port, dispatcher) -> server`` used by tests to\n        substitute the ``python-osc`` server. The returned object must\n        expose ``serve_forever()``, ``shutdown()``, ``server_close()``,\n        and ``handle(addr, *args)`` is *not* required (tests call into\n        the bridge's ``_handle`` directly to avoid the network round\n        trip). When ``None`` (production), the default factory builds\n        ``ThreadingOSCUDPServer`` lazily so importing this module\n        doesn't drag in ``python-osc`` for callers that don't use it.\n    clock : callable, default :func:`time.monotonic`\n        Producer-side timestamp source. Most hardware's OSC packet has\n        no timestamp of its own, so the bridge stamps arrival time —\n        the BPM estimator's One-Euro filter handles small jitter.\n\n    Notes\n    -----\n    The :meth:`stream` iterator pops from the internal queue with a\n    short timeout so :meth:`close` can wake it without leaving the\n    consumer thread blocked.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    source_id: str = \"osc_bridge\"\n    host: str = DEFAULT_BRIDGE_HOST\n    port: int = DEFAULT_BRIDGE_PORT\n    queue_max: int = 4096\n    server_factory: Optional[\n        Callable[[str, int, Any], Any]\n    ] = None\n    clock: Callable[[], float] = field(default=time.monotonic)\n    _queue: \"queue.Queue[IMUSample]\" = field(\n        default_factory=lambda: queue.Queue(maxsize=0), init=False, repr=False\n    )\n    _devices: dict[str, _DeviceState] = field(\n        default_factory=dict, init=False, repr=False\n    )\n    _server: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)\n    _server_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = field(\n        default=None, init=False, repr=False\n    )\n    _stop: threading.Event = field(\n        default_factory=threading.Event, init=False, repr=False\n    )\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.queue_max <= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"queue_max must be positive\")\n        if not isinstance(self.source_id, str) or not self.source_id:\n            raise ValueError(\"source_id must be a non-empty string\")\n        # Recreate the queue with the configured cap; the dataclass field\n        # default is intentionally unbounded because Python dataclasses\n        # need an init-time-frozen default and we want capacity from the\n        # caller's `queue_max`.\n        self._queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=self.queue_max)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # IMUSource Protocol\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def capabilities(self) -> frozenset[str]:\n        # The bridge can carry any capability — pretend we do all of\n        # them because the lookup is per-sample anyway. Returning the\n        # full set lets a Lane Controller register a single bridge as\n        # the freq + accel source for any device that connects later.\n        return frozenset(ALL_CAPABILITIES)\n\n    def open(self) -> None:\n        if self._server is not None:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"OSCImuBridgeAdapter is already open\")\n        self._stop.clear()\n        factory = self.server_factory or _default_server_factory\n        dispatcher = _build_dispatcher(self._handle)\n        self._server = factory(self.host, self.port, dispatcher)\n        if hasattr(self._server, \"serve_forever\"):\n            self._server_thread = threading.Thread(\n                target=self._server.serve_forever,\n                name=f\"OSCImuBridge[{self.host}:{self.port}]\",\n                daemon=True,\n            )\n            self._server_thread.start()\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        # Idempotent: tolerate close() before open() and double-close().\n        self._stop.set()\n        server = self._server\n        self._server = None\n        if server is not None:\n            try:\n                if hasattr(server, \"shutdown\"):\n                    server.shutdown()\n                if hasattr(server, \"server_close\"):\n                    server.server_close()\n            except Exception:\n                # Network teardown should never throw across the abstraction.\n                pass\n        thread = self._server_thread\n        self._server_thread = None\n        if thread is not None and thread.is_alive():\n            thread.join(timeout=1.0)\n\n    def stream(self) -> Iterator[IMUSample]:\n        while not self._stop.is_set():\n            try:\n                sample = self._queue.get(timeout=0.1)\n            except queue.Empty:\n                continue\n            yield sample\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> \"OSCImuBridgeAdapter\":\n        self.open()\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # OSC dispatch (also exposed for unit-test injection)\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def _handle(self, address: str, *args: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Internal handler used by both the production server and tests.\n\n        Tests bypass the UDP path by calling this directly with crafted\n        ``(address, *args)`` tuples, which keeps every assertion\n        deterministic and covers the latching / queue-overflow logic\n        without requiring ``python-osc`` at all.\n        \"\"\"\n        m = _ADDR_RE.match(address)\n        if m is None:\n            return  # not a hw/imu address\n        device = m.group(\"device\")\n        key = m.group(\"key\")\n        state = self._devices.setdefault(device, _DeviceState())\n        now = self.clock()\n        state.last_seen = now\n\n        try:\n            self._update_state(state, key, args)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            # Silently drop malformed packets — the adapter is the buffer\n            # against bad firmware; logging would flood the console on\n            # a misbehaving device.\n            return\n\n        if key in (\"freq\", \"accel\"):\n            sample = self._build_sample(device, state, now)\n            self._enqueue(sample)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _update_state(state: _DeviceState, key: str, args: tuple) -> None:\n        if key == \"accel\":\n            ax, ay, az = (float(args[0]), float(args[1]), float(args[2]))\n            state.last_accel = (ax, ay, az)\n        elif key == \"gyro\":\n            gx, gy, gz = (float(args[0]), float(args[1]), float(args[2]))\n            state.last_gyro = (gx, gy, gz)\n        elif key == \"freq\":\n            freq = float(args[0])\n            conf = float(args[1]) if len(args) > 1 else 1.0\n            state.last_freq_hz = max(0.0, freq)\n            state.last_freq_conf = max(0.0, min(1.0, conf))\n        elif key == \"phase\":\n            state.last_phase = float(args[0]) % 1.0\n        elif key == \"battery\":\n            state.battery = int(args[0])\n        elif key == \"device_kind\":\n            state.device_kind = str(args[0])\n        elif key == \"binding\":\n            state.binding = int(args[0])\n        # FIFO eviction on overflow: drop the oldest sample to make\n        # room rather than block the OSC handler thread (network-bound\n        # producers can't tolerate ms-scale stalls without piling up\n        # firmware-level retransmits).\n        try:\n            self._queue.put_nowait(sample)\n        except queue.Full:\n            try:\n                self._queue.get_nowait()\n            except queue.Empty:\n                pass\n            try:\n                self._queue.put_nowait(sample)\n            except queue.Full:\n                pass\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helpers below the public class — kept module-private so callers stay\n# on the dataclass + Protocol surface.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _build_dispatcher(handler: Callable[..., None]) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Wire a python-osc Dispatcher with a glob match for the prefix.\n\n    Imported lazily so the module is usable in tests / minimal envs\n    that don't install ``python-osc`` (the bridge passes a stub server\n    factory and never reaches this path).\n    \"\"\"\n    from pythonosc.dispatcher import Dispatcher\n\n    d = Dispatcher()\n    d.map(f\"{OSC_HW_PREFIX}/*\", handler, needs_reply_address=False)\n    return d\n\n\ndef _default_server_factory(host: str, port: int, dispatcher: Any) -> Any:\n    from pythonosc.osc_server import ThreadingOSCUDPServer\n\n    return ThreadingOSCUDPServer((host, int(port)), dispatcher)\n\n\n# Sanity assertion: the bridge satisfies the Protocol so a wiring\n# regression in IMUSource shows up at import-time, not deep in the\n# Lane Controller. ``isinstance`` runs the runtime_checkable shape.\nassert isinstance(OSCImuBridgeAdapter(), IMUSource), (  # noqa: S101\n    \"OSCImuBridgeAdapter no longer implements IMUSource — check protocol drift.\"\n)\n_ = (CAPABILITY_ACCEL, CAPABILITY_FREQ, CAPABILITY_GYRO, CAPABILITY_PHASE)\n"

## 错误原因

错误信息直接给了答案：

> `"thinking.type.enabled" is not supported for this model. Use "thinking.type.adaptive" and "output_config.effort"`

Anthropic 在 Opus 4.7 上**移除了**旧的 `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` 格式，**只接受** `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` + `output_config: {effort: "high"}`（参考 [Anthropic 官方文档](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/extended-thinking-models)、[claude-code issue #49219](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/49219)）。

但你 `C:\Users\29989\.claude\settings.json` 里写的是：

```7:14:C:\Users\29989\.claude\settings.json
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME": "Opus 4.7 via Bedrock",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION": "Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES": "effort,xhigh_effort,max_effort,thinking,adaptive_thinking,interleaved_thinking",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL": "high",
```

`SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` 里同时声明了 `thinking` **和** `adaptive_thinking`。按 Claude Code 文档的语义：**列了就启用，不列就禁用**。当 `thinking` 出现时，客户端就允许走旧版的 `enabled` 路径，而你的中转模型 ID `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` 走旧路径会被 Bedrock 直接拒掉。

修法很简单：把 `thinking` 这个 capability 移掉，只保留 `adaptive_thinking`，并加一条兜底 `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY` 强制 adaptive payload。

 我现在看清楚了问题的根本原因和解决方案。用户的 Claude Code v2.1.120 通过 Bedrock 中转服务访问 Opus 4.7 模型，而 settings.json 中同时启用了 `thinking` 和 `adaptive_` 这两个能力声明，这里面存在配置冲突。

Claude Code 检测到 `thinking` 能力后会发送旧版的请求格式（`thinking.type: "enabled"` 加 `budget_tokens`），但 Bedrock 上的 Opus 4.7 已经只支持新格式（`thinking.type: "adaptive"` 加 `output_config.effort`），导致请求被拒绝。

所以我要写一个最小化的流式感知代理，核心功能就是把出站请求中的 `claude-opus-4-7` 改成 `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`，这样 Claude Code 就能通过 pincc 中继访问 Opus 4.7 的 adaptive thinking 功能。

Writing the relay proxy... Continuing the proxy handler to forward the request to the upstream server, rewriting the model ID in the request body if needed, then streaming the response back to the client while handling any errors that occur during transmission.

Now I'm thinking about a potential issue with how HTTP chunked encoding works—when the upstream server returns a chunked response, urllib automatically decodes it into a regular byte stream, but I need to consider whether the client expects the response to remain chunked or if it should be sent as a plain stream for SSE compatibility.

Actually, SSE responses typically have both `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, so I can pass through the SSE content type while letting urllib handle the chunked decoding. The real problem is that without a Content-Length and without chunked encoding (since urllib already decoded it), HTTP/1.1 requires one or the other, which creates an illegal state.

The simplest solution is to add `Connection: close` to the response headers—this way the client will read until the socket closes, which works fine for SSE streams and avoids the Content-Length/chunked dilemma entirely. Since I want to avoid external dependencies on Windows, I'll stick with the standard library and use this approach with urllib.

Now I'm realizing that urllib's streaming with `resp.read(N)` actually handles SSE fine—it reads chunks without buffering the entire response. I'll write a complete implementation that handles streaming SSE passthrough, applies ID translation, and saves it to the project directory. The deployment plan is to run the proxy on port 8765, update the settings to point to it with the standard model ID, and verify that the model translation works by checking the proxy's stdout logs.

```json
{
 "path": "C:\\Users\\29989\\.claude\\tools\\claude_relay.py",
 "contents": "\"\"\"\nTiny localhost relay for Claude Code -> pincc.tamaredge.host.\n\nWhy this exists\n---------------\nClaude Code v2.1.120 on Windows ties its thinking-schema choice to the model\nID's textual prefix. With pincc's Bedrock-style ID\n``global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`` the client refuses to send\n``thinking.type=adaptive`` (regardless of ``_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES``), so\nOpus 4.7 always 400s with \"thinking.type.enabled is not supported\". With the\nplain ID ``claude-opus-4-7`` the client emits adaptive correctly, but pincc's\nmodel registry rejects that ID. This relay bridges both ends:\n\n    Claude Code  --(claude-opus-4-7, adaptive)-->  this relay\n                            |\n                            |  rewrites body model field + thinking shape\n                            v\n                pincc.tamaredge.host  --(global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7,\n                                         adaptive)-->  Bedrock / upstream\n\nSetup\n-----\n1. Run this script (any Python 3.9+):\n       python \"%USERPROFILE%\\\\.claude\\\\tools\\\\claude_relay.py\"\n   It listens on http://***REDACTED-IP***:8765 by default. Add ``--port N`` to change.\n\n2. In ``%USERPROFILE%\\\\.claude\\\\settings.json`` set:\n       \"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL\": \"http://***REDACTED-IP***:8765\"\n       \"ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION\": \"claude-opus-4-7\"\n       \"ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES\":\n           \"effort,xhigh_effort,max_effort,adaptive_thinking,interleaved_thinking\"\n\n3. Restart Claude Code, ``/model`` -> Opus 4.7 via pincc.\n\nThe relay only rewrites; it does no auth and stores no traffic.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport threading\nfrom http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer\nfrom typing import Any\nfrom urllib import error as urlerror\nfrom urllib import request as urlrequest\n\nDEFAULT_UPSTREAM = \"https://pincc.tamaredge.host/api\"\nMODEL_ALIAS = {\n    \"claude-opus-4-7\": \"global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7\",\n}\nHOP_BY_HOP = {\n    \"connection\",\n    \"content-length\",\n    \"host\",\n    \"keep-alive\",\n    \"proxy-authenticate\",\n    \"proxy-authorization\",\n    \"te\",\n    \"trailer\",\n    \"trailers\",\n    \"transfer-encoding\",\n    \"upgrade\",\n}\nEFFORT_FALLBACK = \"high\"\n\n\ndef _coerce_thinking(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Promote legacy ``thinking.type=enabled`` to adaptive in-place.\n\n    Returns True if the body was mutated.\n    \"\"\"\n    thinking = obj.get(\"thinking\")\n    if not isinstance(thinking, dict):\n        return False\n    if thinking.get(\"type\") != \"enabled\":\n        return False\n    thinking[\"type\"] = \"adaptive\"\n    thinking.pop(\"budget_tokens\", None)\n    output_config = obj.get(\"output_config\")\n    if not isinstance(output_config, dict):\n        output_config = {}\n        obj[\"output_config\"] = output_config\n    output_config.setdefault(\"effort\", EFFORT_FALLBACK)\n    return True\n\n\ndef rewrite_body(raw: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Apply model-ID and thinking-schema rewrites. Returns (body, notes).\"\"\"\n    if not raw:\n        return raw, []\n    try:\n        obj = json.loads(raw)\n    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):\n        return raw, []\n    notes: list[str] = []\n    model = obj.get(\"model\")\n    if isinstance(model, str) and model in MODEL_ALIAS:\n        obj[\"model\"] = MODEL_ALIAS[model]\n        notes.append(f\"model: {model} -> {obj['model']}\")\n    if _coerce_thinking(obj):\n        notes.append(\"thinking: enabled -> adaptive\")\n    if not notes:\n        return raw, notes\n    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\"), notes\n\n\nclass RelayHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):\n    upstream: str = DEFAULT_UPSTREAM\n    timeout: float = 600.0\n    protocol_version = \"HTTP/1.1\"\n\n    def _forward(self, method: str) -> None:\n        length = int(self.headers.get(\"Content-Length\", \"0\") or \"0\")\n        body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b\"\"\n        body, notes = rewrite_body(body)\n\n        upstream_url = self.upstream + self.path\n        req = urlrequest.Request(upstream_url, data=body or None, method=method)\n        for k, v in self.headers.items():\n            if k.lower() in HOP_BY_HOP:\n                continue\n            req.add_header(k, v)\n        if body:\n            req.add_header(\"Content-Length\", str(len(body)))\n\n        if notes:\n            sys.stderr.write(f\"[relay] {method} {self.path} :: {', '.join(notes)}\\n\")\n\n        try:\n            resp = urlrequest.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout)\n        except urlerror.HTTPError as exc:\n            payload = exc.read() or b\"\"\n            self.send_response(exc.code)\n            for k, v in exc.headers.items():\n                if k.lower() in HOP_BY_HOP:\n                    continue\n                self.send_header(k, v)\n            self.send_header(\"Content-Length\", str(len(payload)))\n            self.send_header(\"Connection\", \"close\")\n            self.end_headers()\n            if payload:\n                try:\n                    self.wfile.write(payload)\n                except OSError:\n                    pass\n            return\n        except urlerror.URLError as exc:\n            self._send_text(502, f\"upstream connect error: {exc}\")\n            return\n        except Exception as exc:\n            self._send_text(502, f\"relay error: {exc}\")\n            return\n\n        try:\n            self.send_response(resp.status)\n            for k, v in resp.headers.items():\n                if k.lower() in HOP_BY_HOP:\n                    continue\n                self.send_header(k, v)\n            self.send_header(\"Connection\", \"close\")\n            self.end_headers()\n            while True:\n                chunk = resp.read(4096)\n                if not chunk:\n                    break\n                try:\n                    self.wfile.write(chunk)\n                    self.wfile.flush()\n                except OSError:\n                    break\n        finally:\n            resp.close()\n\n    def _send_text(self, status: int, msg: str) -> None:\n        body = msg.encode(\"utf-8\")\n        self.send_response(status)\n        self.send_header(\"Content-Type\", \"text/plain; charset=utf-8\")\n        self.send_header(\"Content-Length\", str(len(body)))\n        self.send_header(\"Connection\", \"close\")\n        self.end_headers()\n        try:\n            self.wfile.write(body)\n        except OSError:\n            pass\n\n    def do_GET(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"GET\")\n\n    def do_POST(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"POST\")\n\n    def do_PUT(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"PUT\")\n\n    def do_DELETE(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"DELETE\")\n\n    def do_PATCH(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"PATCH\")\n\n    def do_OPTIONS(self) -> None:\n        self._forward(\"OPTIONS\")\n\n    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:\n        sys.stderr.write(f\"[relay] {self.address_string()} {fmt % args}\\n\")\n\n\ndef serve(bind: str, port: int, upstream: str) -> None:\n    RelayHandler.upstream = upstream.rstrip(\"/\")\n    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((bind, port), RelayHandler)\n    sys.stderr.write(\n        f\"[relay] listening on http://{bind}:{port} -> {RelayHandler.upstream}\\n\"\n    )\n    sys.stderr.write(f\"[relay] model alias: {MODEL_ALIAS}\\n\")\n    sys.stderr.flush()\n    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()\n    try:\n        while True:\n            sys.stdin.read(1) if not sys.stdin.closed else threading.Event().wait(60)\n    except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):\n        pass\n    finally:\n        server.shutdown()\n        server.server_close()\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Localhost relay for Claude Code\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--bind\", default=\"***REDACTED-IP***\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8765)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--upstream\", default=DEFAULT_UPSTREAM)\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    serve(args.bind, args.port, args.upstream)\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}
```
