 "new_string": "def hip_y(lm, vis_threshold: float = 0.0):\n    \"\"\"Per-frame hip-midpoint ``y`` coordinate.\n\n    Uses OpenCV pixel convention where ``y`` grows downward — a *larger*\n    ``hip_y`` means the subject sank lower on screen (i.e. a squat).\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    lm : array_like, shape ``(T, 33, 4)`` or ``(33, 4)``\n    vis_threshold : float, default 0.0\n        A hip whose visibility is below this value is treated as missing\n        and does not participate in the left/right average. When both\n        hips fall below the threshold the output is ``NaN``. ``0.0``\n        disables the gate.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    np.ndarray\n        Shape ``(T,)`` (or scalar for a single frame).\n    \"\"\"\n    lm = np.asarray(lm, dtype=np.float64)\n    ys = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_HIP, _MP_RIGHT_HIP], 1]\n    if vis_threshold > 0.0:\n        vis = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_HIP, _MP_RIGHT_HIP], 3]\n        ys = np.where(vis < vis_threshold, np.nan, ys)\n    with warnings.catch_warnings(), np.errstate(invalid=\"ignore\"):\n        warnings.simplefilter(\"ignore\", category=RuntimeWarning)\n        return np.nanmean(ys, axis=-1)\n\n\ndef shoulder_width(lm, vis_threshold: float = 0.0):\n    \"\"\"Per-frame shoulder-to-shoulder horizontal distance (px).\n\n    Used as a body-scale normaliser by the jumping-jack detector — every\n    person's \"fully open\" arm/leg spread is roughly proportional to their\n    shoulder width regardless of camera distance.\n\n    Returns ``NaN`` when either shoulder is missing or below the\n    visibility threshold.\n    \"\"\"\n    lm = np.asarray(lm, dtype=np.float64)\n    xs = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_SHOULDER, _MP_RIGHT_SHOULDER], 0]\n    if vis_threshold > 0.0:\n        vis = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_SHOULDER, _MP_RIGHT_SHOULDER], 3]\n        xs = np.where(vis < vis_threshold, np.nan, xs)\n    return np.abs(xs[..., 0] - xs[..., 1])\n\n\ndef arm_spread_y(lm, vis_threshold: float = 0.0):\n    \"\"\"Per-frame \"wrists raised over shoulders\" amount (px).\n\n    SPEC §6.2.2 calls this ``wrist_to_shoulder_vertical``. Implemented as\n    the **mean** vertical lift of the two wrists relative to their\n    same-side shoulder, in pixel-y. OpenCV ``y`` grows downward so the\n    sign convention is flipped: ``arm_spread_y = mean(shoulder_y -\n    wrist_y)``. A wrist held above the shoulder yields a *positive*\n    value; arms at rest at the side hover near zero / slightly negative.\n\n    Using the bilateral mean (instead of ``min`` / ``max``) tolerates a\n    one-sided arm raise (a wave, a grab) without misreading it as a full\n    jumping-jack. NaN-tolerant — missing wrists or shoulders fall out via\n    :func:`numpy.nanmean`.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    np.ndarray\n        Shape ``(T,)`` (or scalar). ``NaN`` only when *both* arms are\n        missing the same frame.\n    \"\"\"\n    lm = np.asarray(lm, dtype=np.float64)\n    sh = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_SHOULDER, _MP_RIGHT_SHOULDER], 1]\n    wr = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_WRIST, _MP_RIGHT_WRIST], 1]\n    if vis_threshold > 0.0:\n        sh_v = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_SHOULDER, _MP_RIGHT_SHOULDER], 3]\n        wr_v = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_WRIST, _MP_RIGHT_WRIST], 3]\n        sh = np.where(sh_v < vis_threshold, np.nan, sh)\n        wr = np.where(wr_v < vis_threshold, np.nan, wr)\n    lift = sh - wr  # +y = wrist above shoulder\n    with warnings.catch_warnings(), np.errstate(invalid=\"ignore\"):\n        warnings.simplefilter(\"ignore\", category=RuntimeWarning)\n        return np.nanmean(lift, axis=-1)\n\n\ndef ankle_distance_x(lm, vis_threshold: float = 0.0):\n    \"\"\"Per-frame absolute horizontal distance between ankles (px).\n\n    SPEC §6.2.2 ``ankle_horizontal_distance``. Closed legs (a tight\n    stance, the bottom of a jumping-jack) give a small value; opened\n    legs (top of a jumping-jack) give a large one.\n\n    Returns ``NaN`` when either ankle is missing or below the visibility\n    threshold — it's misleading to report \"0 px\" for an unobserved leg.\n    \"\"\"\n    lm = np.asarray(lm, dtype=np.float64)\n    xs = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_ANKLE, _MP_RIGHT_ANKLE], 0]\n    if vis_threshold > 0.0:\n        vis = lm[..., [_MP_LEFT_ANKLE, _MP_RIGHT_ANKLE], 3]\n        xs = np.where(vis < vis_threshold, np.nan, xs)\n    return np.abs(xs[..., 0] - xs[..., 1])\n\n\ndef count_zero_crossings(x) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Number of mean-crossing sign flips in 1-D series ``x``.\n\n    Centres ``x`` on its own mean (so any DC offset disappears), then\n    counts the sign flips of the resulting sequence. NaN samples are\n    dropped *before* centering so a few missing frames in the middle of\n    a real cycle do not skew the mean. A series with fewer than two\n    finite samples returns ``0`` — there's no \"cycle\" to speak of.\n\n    Used by the rule-based detectors as a cheap periodicity proxy: one\n    full down-up cycle of a body signal traverses its mean twice, hence\n    the typical ``count_zero_crossings(...) >= 2`` gate (SPEC §6.2.2).\n    \"\"\"\n    arr = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)\n    finite = arr[np.isfinite(arr)]\n    if finite.size < 2:\n        return 0\n    centered = finite - np.mean(finite)\n    signs = np.sign(centered)\n    signs = signs[signs != 0]\n    if signs.size < 2:\n        return 0\n    return int(np.sum(np.diff(signs) != 0))\n\n\ndef correlation_coef(x, y) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Pearson correlation of two 1-D series, NaN-tolerant.\n\n    SPEC §6.2.2 uses this to gate jumping-jack on the arm-and-leg\n    *in-phase* condition: arms going up while legs go out yields ``corr\n    > 0.5``; flailing one limb while the other stays still drops below.\n\n    Returns ``NaN`` when fewer than 4 paired finite samples remain\n    (anything less is statistically noise) or when either series is\n    constant on the overlap (``denom == 0``).\n    \"\"\"\n    a = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64).ravel()\n    b = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).ravel()\n    if a.shape != b.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"correlation_coef: shape mismatch {a.shape} vs {b.shape}\"\n        )\n    mask = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)\n    if int(mask.sum()) < 4:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    ac = a[mask] - np.mean(a[mask])\n    bc = b[mask] - np.mean(b[mask])\n    denom = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(ac * ac) * np.sum(bc * bc)))\n    if denom == 0.0:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return float(np.sum(ac * bc) / denom)"
}

 "contents": "\"\"\"\nRule-based jumping-jack detector (SPEC §6.2.2).\n\nDirect port of the pseudocode::\n\n    def detect_jumping_jack(lm):\n        arm_spread = wrist_to_shoulder_vertical(lm)    # 腕高过肩时为正\n        leg_spread = ankle_horizontal_distance(lm)     # 踝间距\n        corr = correlation_coef(arm_spread, leg_spread)\n        both_cycle = is_periodic(arm_spread) and is_periodic(leg_spread)\n        is_active = both_cycle and corr > 0.5\n        form = clip01(min(arm_spread.max(),\n                          leg_spread.max() / shoulder_width(lm)))\n        return is_active, corr, form\n\nDifferences from the spec\n-------------------------\n1. **Form normalisation**. SPEC writes\n   ``min(arm_spread.max(), leg_spread.max() / shoulder_width(lm))`` which\n   compares a raw pixel quantity with a unit-less ratio — the units do\n   not match. We normalise *both* signals by shoulder width before\n   taking the ``min``. Empirically a fully-open jumping jack reaches\n   ``arm_lift ≈ 1.0 × shoulder_width`` (wrists raised one shoulder above\n   their resting line) and ``ankle_gap ≈ 1.6 × shoulder_width``, so we\n   divide each peak by its own target and clamp the smaller one to\n   ``[0, 1]``. This is the only clean way to keep ``form`` invariant to\n   how far the subject stands from the camera.\n\n2. **NaN tolerance**. Landmarks may be missing for frames where the\n   subject leaves the frame; ``pose_mapping`` fills unmapped MP slots\n   with NaN. The geometry primitives already propagate NaN, but we\n   guard against an \"all NaN\" buffer up-front so the first ~2 s of\n   tracking does not report spurious \"active\" frames before the\n   rolling buffer fills.\n\n3. **Periodicity gate**. SPEC's ``is_periodic`` is left unspecified. We\n   apply the same ``count_zero_crossings(...) >= MIN_HALF_CYCLES`` rule\n   that the squat detector uses on hip_y, with ``MIN_HALF_CYCLES = 2``\n   so a single slow open-and-close inside the 2 s window already\n   counts. Two complete jacks bank ``hip_cycles == 4``; one shaky half\n   bank stays at ``< 2`` and is rejected.\n\n4. **Confidence vs correlation**. SPEC returns ``corr`` as the second\n   value. We pass ``confidence = clip01(corr)`` instead because the\n   raw Pearson coefficient can land in ``[-1, 1]`` and would force the\n   arbitration helper to special-case negative numbers. Negative\n   correlation simply means \"arms and legs out of phase\" → not a\n   jumping jack.\n\n5. **Insufficient data**. When the buffer holds fewer than\n   ``MIN_VALID_FRAMES`` finite samples for either signal, we bail out\n   with ``(False, 0.0, 0.0)`` rather than letting a tiny sample produce\n   a high-variance correlation by accident.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom python.utils.geometry import (\n    ankle_distance_x,\n    arm_spread_y,\n    clip01,\n    correlation_coef,\n    count_zero_crossings,\n    shoulder_width,\n)\n\nMIN_CORR: float = 0.5\n\"\"\"Pearson correlation between arm_spread and leg_spread to claim \"in phase\".\"\"\"\n\nMIN_HALF_CYCLES: int = 2\n\"\"\"``count_zero_crossings`` floor that means \"the signal is actually moving\".\"\"\"\n\nMIN_VALID_FRAMES: int = 20\n\"\"\"<20 finite frames in either signal → window treated as unobserved.\"\"\"\n\nARM_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO: float = 1.0\n\"\"\"Wrists raised this many shoulder-widths above their shoulders → arm_form = 1.\n\nSPEC §6.2.2 doesn't pin a number; 1.0 matches a \"wrists overhead, arms\nfully outstretched\" jumping jack on a typical adult body plan and\nchecks against synthetic data without false-saturating low-effort raises.\n\"\"\"\n\nLEG_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO: float = 1.6\n\"\"\"Ankle gap this many shoulder-widths apart → leg_form = 1.\n\nA standing-stance jumping jack lands at roughly 1.5–1.7× shoulder\nwidth; 1.6 is the midpoint and lines up with the synthetic fixtures\nused in :mod:`tools._smoke_pipeline`.\n\"\"\"\n\nMIN_SHOULDER_WIDTH_PX: float = 1.0\n\"\"\"Below this the body-scale denominator is unreliable → form = 0.0.\n\nCamera-rotated edge cases (subject lying down, near-zero parallax)\ncollapse shoulder width to a few pixels; without this gate the form\nratio explodes. Practically rare but defended explicitly to match the\n\"fails closed\" pattern in :mod:`python.action.squat`.\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass JumpingJackFeatures:\n    \"\"\"Intermediate quantities (exposed for HUD / unit tests).\"\"\"\n\n    arm_spread: np.ndarray\n    leg_spread: np.ndarray\n    corr: float\n    arm_cycles: int\n    leg_cycles: int\n    arm_peak_px: float\n    leg_peak_px: float\n    shoulder_width_px: float\n    usable_arm_frames: int\n    usable_leg_frames: int\n\n\ndef jumping_jack_features(lm: np.ndarray) -> JumpingJackFeatures:\n    \"\"\"Compute the per-window signals SPEC §6.2.2 feeds into the decision.\"\"\"\n    lm = np.asarray(lm, dtype=np.float64)\n    arm = arm_spread_y(lm)\n    leg = ankle_distance_x(lm)\n    sw_series = shoulder_width(lm)\n\n    usable_arm = int(np.sum(np.isfinite(arm)))\n    usable_leg = int(np.sum(np.isfinite(leg)))\n    if usable_arm == 0 or usable_leg == 0:\n        return JumpingJackFeatures(\n            arm_spread=arm,\n            leg_spread=leg,\n            corr=float(\"nan\"),\n            arm_cycles=0,\n            leg_cycles=0,\n            arm_peak_px=0.0,\n            leg_peak_px=0.0,\n            shoulder_width_px=float(\"nan\"),\n            usable_arm_frames=usable_arm,\n            usable_leg_frames=usable_leg,\n        )\n\n    corr = correlation_coef(arm, leg)\n    arm_cycles = count_zero_crossings(arm)\n    leg_cycles = count_zero_crossings(leg)\n    arm_peak = float(np.nanmax(arm))\n    leg_peak = float(np.nanmax(leg))\n    sw = float(np.nanmean(sw_series))\n\n    return JumpingJackFeatures(\n        arm_spread=arm,\n        leg_spread=leg,\n        corr=corr,\n        arm_cycles=arm_cycles,\n        leg_cycles=leg_cycles,\n        arm_peak_px=arm_peak,\n        leg_peak_px=leg_peak,\n        shoulder_width_px=sw,\n        usable_arm_frames=usable_arm,\n        usable_leg_frames=usable_leg,\n    )\n\n\ndef detect_jumping_jack(lm: np.ndarray) -> tuple[bool, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"SPEC §6.2.2 jumping-jack detector.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    lm : np.ndarray\n        Shape ``(T, 33, 4)``. ``T`` is typically 60 (a 2 s buffer at 30 fps).\n        Layout follows :mod:`python.pose_mapping`; missing slots are NaN.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    is_active : bool\n    confidence : float\n        ``clip01(corr)``. Negative correlation collapses to 0.\n    form_score : float\n        ``clip01(min(arm_lift / shoulder_width / ARM_TARGET,\n                     ankle_gap / shoulder_width / LEG_TARGET))``.\n    \"\"\"\n    feats = jumping_jack_features(lm)\n\n    if (\n        feats.usable_arm_frames < MIN_VALID_FRAMES\n        or feats.usable_leg_frames < MIN_VALID_FRAMES\n    ):\n        return False, 0.0, 0.0\n\n    is_active = bool(\n        feats.arm_cycles >= MIN_HALF_CYCLES\n        and feats.leg_cycles >= MIN_HALF_CYCLES\n        and np.isfinite(feats.corr)\n        and feats.corr > MIN_CORR\n    )\n\n    confidence = float(clip01(feats.corr if np.isfinite(feats.corr) else 0.0))\n\n    if (\n        not np.isfinite(feats.shoulder_width_px)\n        or feats.shoulder_width_px < MIN_SHOULDER_WIDTH_PX\n    ):\n        form = 0.0\n    else:\n        arm_norm = feats.arm_peak_px / feats.shoulder_width_px / ARM_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO\n        leg_norm = feats.leg_peak_px / feats.shoulder_width_px / LEG_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO\n        form = float(clip01(min(arm_norm, leg_norm)))\n\n    return is_active, confidence, form\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"detect_jumping_jack\",\n    \"jumping_jack_features\",\n    \"JumpingJackFeatures\",\n    \"MIN_CORR\",\n    \"MIN_HALF_CYCLES\",\n    \"MIN_VALID_FRAMES\",\n    \"ARM_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO\",\n    \"LEG_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO\",\n    \"MIN_SHOULDER_WIDTH_PX\",\n]\n"

Then I'm verifying the arbitration logic classifies jumping jack frames correctly, with the test parameters using 60 frames across 2 complete cycles to ensure the phase stepping captures the full motion.

Now I'm thinking through the zero-crossing logic: a raised cosine signal (which represents arm spread) oscillates from 0 to 1 and back, so after removing the mean it crosses zero twice per cycle. With 2 jumping jack cycles, that's 4 zero crossings total, which satisfies the minimum threshold. The arm spread signal itself swings negative when arms are closed and positive when open, producing the same crossing pattern. This all checks out theoretically.

Now I need to create a test case where only the arms move while the legs stay still—this should fail detection since there won't be any leg cycles detected.

Setting up helper function for arms-only motion... I need to verify the MP33 landmark mappings are correct—the arm spread, ankle distance, and shoulder width calculations all depend on specific COCO keypoint indices, and I'm confirming that the existing conversion function properly maps those points. Everything checks out, so now I'm ready to write tests for this new synthesis function.

 "new_string": "def _squat_window(troughs: list[float], n_frames: int = 60) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Build a (T, 33, 4) MP-33 buffer simulating ``troughs`` full cycles.\"\"\"\n    if not troughs:\n        return np.full((n_frames, MP33_NUM_LANDMARKS, 4), np.nan, dtype=np.float64)\n\n    per_cycle = max(4, n_frames // len(troughs))\n    angles: list[float] = []\n    for t in troughs:\n        for i in range(per_cycle):\n            phase = 2 * math.pi * i / (per_cycle - 1)\n            half = (1 - math.cos(phase)) / 2\n            angles.append(170.0 - (170.0 - t) * half)\n    # pad / clip to n_frames\n    while len(angles) < n_frames:\n        angles.append(170.0)\n    angles = angles[:n_frames]\n\n    mp33 = np.empty((n_frames, MP33_NUM_LANDMARKS, 4), dtype=np.float64)\n    for i, ang in enumerate(angles):\n        coco = _person_coco17(ang)[None, ...]  # (1, 17, 2)\n        mp33[i] = coco17_to_mp33(coco)[0]\n    return mp33\n\n\ndef _person_coco17_jj(\n    arm_open: float,\n    leg_open: float | None = None,\n    center: tuple[float, float] = (320.0, 240.0),\n) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Synthesise a (17, 2) COCO tensor of a jumping-jack at the given openness.\n\n    ``arm_open`` and ``leg_open`` (defaulting to ``arm_open``) live in\n    ``[0, 1]``: 0 = arms-down + feet-together (closed), 1 = arms-overhead +\n    feet-wide (fully open). Numbers chosen so a fully-open frame produces\n\n    * arm_spread_y ≈ +60 px       (wrists 60 px above shoulders)\n    * ankle_distance_x ≈ 1.6 × shoulder_width\n    * shoulder_width ≈ 60 px\n\n    matching :data:`python.action.jumping_jack.ARM_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO`\n    and ``LEG_SPREAD_TARGET_RATIO`` so the form score saturates near\n    1.0 on a clean cycle.\n    \"\"\"\n    cx, cy_ref = center\n    a = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(arm_open)))\n    g = a if leg_open is None else max(0.0, min(1.0, float(leg_open)))\n\n    sw = 60.0\n    sh_y = cy_ref - 80.0\n    left_shoulder = (cx - sw / 2.0, sh_y)\n    right_shoulder = (cx + sw / 2.0, sh_y)\n\n    # Wrist y: closed = 70 px below shoulder (arms at sides, hands by hips)\n    # Open    = 60 px above shoulder (wrists overhead)\n    wrist_y_closed = sh_y + 70.0\n    wrist_y_open = sh_y - 60.0\n    wrist_y = wrist_y_closed + (wrist_y_open - wrist_y_closed) * a\n\n    # Wrist x: stays a touch outside the shoulder line. We don't model the\n    # full lateral sweep because the detector reads the *vertical* lift\n    # via :func:`arm_spread_y`; horizontal arm motion would only matter\n    # for a future arm-cycle detector.\n    wrist_x_offset = 50.0\n    left_wrist = (cx - wrist_x_offset, wrist_y)\n    right_wrist = (cx + wrist_x_offset, wrist_y)\n\n    # Elbows mid-segment so the rendered skeleton stays plausible (the\n    # detector itself doesn't read elbows).\n    left_elbow = (\n        (left_shoulder[0] + left_wrist[0]) / 2.0,\n        (left_shoulder[1] + left_wrist[1]) / 2.0,\n    )\n    right_elbow = (\n        (right_shoulder[0] + right_wrist[0]) / 2.0,\n        (right_shoulder[1] + right_wrist[1]) / 2.0,\n    )\n\n    # Ankle gap: 20 px closed -> ~96 px open (≈ 1.6 × sw). Knees mid-segment.\n    ankle_gap_closed = 20.0\n    ankle_gap_open = 96.0\n    ankle_gap = ankle_gap_closed + (ankle_gap_open - ankle_gap_closed) * g\n    ankle_y = cy_ref + 120.0\n    left_ankle = (cx - ankle_gap / 2.0, ankle_y)\n    right_ankle = (cx + ankle_gap / 2.0, ankle_y)\n\n    left_hip = (cx - 5.0, cy_ref)\n    right_hip = (cx + 5.0, cy_ref)\n    left_knee = ((left_hip[0] + left_ankle[0]) / 2.0, (left_hip[1] + left_ankle[1]) / 2.0)\n    right_knee = (\n        (right_hip[0] + right_ankle[0]) / 2.0,\n        (right_hip[1] + right_ankle[1]) / 2.0,\n    )\n\n    nose = (cx, cy_ref - 100.0)\n    left_eye = (cx - 5.0, cy_ref - 105.0)\n    right_eye = (cx + 5.0, cy_ref - 105.0)\n    left_ear = (cx - 10.0, cy_ref - 100.0)\n    right_ear = (cx + 10.0, cy_ref - 100.0)\n\n    pts = [\n        nose, left_eye, right_eye, left_ear, right_ear,\n        left_shoulder, right_shoulder, left_elbow, right_elbow,\n        left_wrist, right_wrist,\n        left_hip, right_hip, left_knee, right_knee,\n        left_ankle, right_ankle,\n    ]\n    return np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.float64)\n\n\ndef _jumping_jack_window(\n    n_cycles: int,\n    n_frames: int = 60,\n    *,\n    leg_lock: float | None = None,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Build a (T, 33, 4) MP-33 buffer simulating ``n_cycles`` full jacks.\n\n    ``leg_lock`` overrides the leg-spread parameter so we can synthesise\n    \"arms only\" footage (legs glued shut) for the false-positive test.\n    Pass ``None`` (default) to keep arms and legs in sync.\n    \"\"\"\n    if n_cycles <= 0:\n        coco = _person_coco17_jj(0.0, leg_open=leg_lock if leg_lock is not None else 0.0)\n        coco = coco[None, ...]\n        mp33 = np.tile(coco17_to_mp33(coco), (n_frames, 1, 1))\n        return mp33\n\n    per_cycle = max(4, n_frames // n_cycles)\n    open_series: list[float] = []\n    for _ in range(n_cycles):\n        for i in range(per_cycle):\n            phase = 2 * math.pi * i / (per_cycle - 1)\n            half = (1 - math.cos(phase)) / 2  # 0 -> 1 -> 0\n            open_series.append(half)\n    while len(open_series) < n_frames:\n        open_series.append(0.0)\n    open_series = open_series[:n_frames]\n\n    mp33 = np.empty((n_frames, MP33_NUM_LANDMARKS, 4), dtype=np.float64)\n    for i, a in enumerate(open_series):\n        coco = _person_coco17_jj(a, leg_open=leg_lock if leg_lock is not None else None)\n        coco = coco[None, ...]\n        mp33[i] = coco17_to_mp33(coco)[0]\n    return mp33"

### 👤 用户

> 不是我的意思是不同乐器有自己音节密度就对于了不同运动类型的节奏，因为不是所有运动都是同一个频率的。比如战绳可以快一点深蹲就可以慢一点

### 🤖 Agent

你的两句话我合起来理解一下，看是不是：

> 不同动作天然有不同 BPM 区间（战绳快 / 深蹲慢）→ 不同乐器的"音节密度"也不一样（贝斯稀疏适合慢、鼓 hi-hat 密集适合快）→ 所以**每个动作对应它最合适的乐器节奏**，而不是所有乐器都跑同一个数字。

但同一句话有两种合理实现，差别很大。我需要你二选一才能改 plan：

 用户澄清了他的真实意图——不是在讨论音乐学中的音符密度倍数关系，而是在说不同运动类型天然对应不同伴奏乐器的节奏密度。战绳这种快速运动需要密集的鼓点节奏来匹配。

深蹲这种慢速运动则需要稀疏的贝斯长音。每种动作都有自己的 BPM 范围和最适配的主导乐器——这就是"音节密度"的真正含义。

现在我明白了，用户说的不是音乐学里的音符倍数关系，而是**动作类型直接决定乐器选择**。所以规划应该是：每个动作绑定一个主导乐器（深蹲配贝斯、开合跳配鼓、拳击配吉他、高抬腿配 hi-hat），学员的运动 BPM 就直接成为整首歌的 master BPM，主导乐器跟着这个 BPM 走。

但这又和用户之前说的"150 BPM 不等于所有乐器都是 150"产生了矛盾——我需要重新理解这两句话的真实含义：第一句是说 master BPM 不决定每个乐器的触发频率，第二句是说不同运动本身就有不同的自然频率。合并起来的逻辑应该是学员的深蹲频率成为 master，但各乐器的音节密度各自独立。

我现在看到了关键点：**同一个乐器在不同动作下的音节密度（note_value）是不同的**——深蹲时鼓走 2.0 倍数让节奏不显得太慢，开合跳时鼓走 1.0 倍数因为动作本身已经很快了，这样才能既保持音乐的完整性，又让每个乐器的表现适配当前的运动节奏。 我意识到用户想要的其实是：每个动作有自己的 BPM 区间，对应一组乐器组合，这些乐器同时演奏但各自的音节密度不同——深蹲用低频密度的贝斯为主，战绳用高频密集的鼓为主。这样既保留了多声部的完整音乐感，又让每个动作的乐器配置反映其运动特性。

我需要在设计方案中明确每个动作的主导乐器和配角乐器的 note_value 比例，确保配角乐器的实际 BPM 落在它们各自的舒适区间内，或者直接问用户是否只需要一动作一乐器的简化版本。

不过用户已经多次表达了"完整音乐"的想法，我应该尊重这个方向，但还是需要确认一个关键问题：是让多个乐器同时响（每个乐器通过 note_value 调整到自己的舒适 BPM），还是简单地根据当前动作切换唯一的主乐器。前者更复杂但音乐感更完整，后者更直观但可能显得单调。我应该直接问这个二选一。

首先要确定每个动作的乐器舒适区和 profile 设计逻辑——深蹲用贝斯主导配合鼓吉他，开合跳用鼓主导，拳击用吉他或主奏主导，高抬腿用鼓 hi-hat 主导。关键是 note_value 的设计原则：让每个 voice 根据 master BPM 动态调整，落在自己的舒适区内，比如鼓的舒适区是 80-180 BPM，当 master 变化时，通过调整 note_value 来保持鼓的实际 BPM 在舒适范围。

实现上有两条路：一是在 profile 里写死 note_value，简单但可能在边界情况下让 voice 飘出舒适区；二是给每个 voice 设定 comfort_min/comfort_max，运行时动态计算 note_value 来保证 voice_bpm 落在舒适区内，这样音乐性更好但实现复杂。我倾向先用静态 note_value 的方案，配置得当的话也能满足需求。

动作切换时，profile 会跟着切换，master BPM source 重置，多个 voice 的 OSC 同步切换。PD 端处理很简单——每次发新的 lane BPM，metro 自然跟新值，不响的 voice 通过 gain=0 静音。webcam_pose_preview 那边需要注意的是，当 active_rep_action 切换时，旧 profile 的 voice 应该 gain=0 静音，新 profile 的 voice 启动。

最终的 plan 结构是在 Python 端建立 song_profile.py，定义 InstrumentVoice 和 ActionSongProfile 类，为 4 个动作各配置一个 profile，每个 profile 的 voice 配置对应 SPEC 的乐器适配建议，然后实现一个函数来根据 master BPM 计算各 voice 的实际 BPM。

webcam_pose_preview.py 增加 song-mode，启用时检测稳定动作选择 profile，通过 4 个 LaneOscSender 分别发送各 lane 的 BPM、乐器、反馈和动作信息，对其他 3 个动作的 lane 发送 gain=0 静音，同时在 HUD 显示 master BPM 和各 voice 当前 BPM，动作切换时平滑过渡旧新 profile 的 voice gain，本地音频跟随当前 profile 的主导 lane。fake_multi_lane_sender.py 增强参数支持按 profile 多 lane 发送。

- lane 2 = `bass`
- lane 3 = `guitar`
- lane 4 = `lead`

`drums=75`、`bass=37.5`、`guitar=37.5`、`lead=75`。

UI 布局（BigScreen.vue）\n\n``​`\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  MasterHud: BPM 124.0  ▮ section: warmup  ▮ EXPECTED: SQUAT  │\n├────────────┬────────────┬────────────┬────────────────────────┤\n│  LANE 1    │  LANE 2    │  LANE 3    │  LANE 4                │\n│  drums     │  bass      │  WAITING   │  WAITING               │\n│  ┌──────┐  │  ┌──────┐  │            │                        │\n│  │BADGE:│  │  │BADGE:│  │            │                        │\n│  │SQUAT │  │  │  —   │  │            │                        │\n│  ├──────┤  │  ├──────┤  │            │                        │\n│  │      │  │  │      │  │            │                        │\n│  │ Rail │  │  │ Rail │  │            │                        │\n│  │      │  │  │      │  │            │                        │\n│  └──────┘  │  └──────┘  │            │                        │\n│  Δ BPM     │  Δ BPM     │            │                        │\n│  +1.2 ●    │  -- ●      │            │                        │\n│  FORM ▆▆▆▂ │  FORM ▁    │            │                        │\n└────────────┴────────────┴────────────┴────────────────────────┘\n``​`\n\n不匹配时整个 lane 列加 8px 红色边框 + 顶部覆盖 \"Expected: Jumping Jack\"（SPEC §6.2.4）。\n\n## 7. 风险与对策\n\n- **OSC mirror 丢包**：UDP 不保证；选 5006 仅在本机回环，丢包率极低；ws_hub 的 30Hz 广播本身就是节流，丢一两个 OSC 不致命。\n- **WebSocket 重连**：useLanesSocket 写指数退避（500ms→2s→4s→8s）。\n- **Canvas 性能**：4 个 BeatRail × 60fps，每个画 < 50 个图元，远在浏览器预算内。\n- **lane 2-4 占位**：当前 webcam 是单人 `max_det=1`；BigScreen 收到 lane_id=1 的快照后只激活 lane 1，其余显示 \"WAITING\"，不依赖多人代码。\n- **前端构建依赖**：要求 Node 18+ 与 pnpm/npm；docs 中明示。\n\n## 8. 验收标准\n\n每个 todo 完成后必须能通过下面的某项手动验证（按顺序）：\n\n1. 中转**完全可达**，但 token **以错误的 header 形式发送**。原因：
- 你用的是 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`，Claude Code SDK 会把它当 OAuth bearer / 内部走自己的认证流程
- 而 PinCC 中转只认 `x-api-key: cr_…` 这种标准 API key 形式

我手动用 `x-api-key` 直打 `/v1/messages` 那次能跑通，就是因为用了正确的 header。

**修复方法：把环境变量名从 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` 改为 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`**。

先杀进程，再改配置。

 啊，问题找到了！Claude Code CLI 每次请求都收到 `401 Invalid API key format` 错误并在重试，这说明中转本身是工作的（我之前用 PowerShell 直接调 `/v1/messages` 成功过），但 CLI 在对接时发送 API key 的格式不对。我用 PowerShell 成功是因为用了 `x-api-key` header，所以关键是 CLI 需要用同样的方式来传递密钥。

问题在于 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` 会被发送为 `Authorization: Bearer` 格式，而中转可能要求 `x-api-key` 或特定的 token 前缀，所以我需要把环境变量改成 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`，这样 CLI 就会用 `x-api-key` header 来发送，跟我 PowerShell 成功的方式保持一致。

我还注意到 debug 日志显示没有 Authorization header，但服务端报"Invalid API key format"，这可能意味着 token 的格式或前缀有问题——虽然我用 `cr_…` 手动调 `/v1/messages` 是成功的，所以问题应该不在 token 本身。

差异可能在于 CLI 用的是某种内部 OAuth 流程来处理 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN，而 PinCC 中转不支持这种方式。最直接的解决办法就是改用 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 并通过 `x-api-key` header 发送，然后杀掉卡住的进程重新尝试。

bars_left: number } | null\n+  }\n+  lanes: Record<string, LaneState>\n+}\n+\n+interface LaneState {\n+  lane_id: number\n+  bpm: number | null\n+  phase: number | null\n+  delta_bpm: number\n+  detune_cents: number\n+  gain: number\n+  action: string\n+  action_confidence: number\n+  form_score: number\n+  rep_count: number\n+  action_match: boolean\n+  off_beat_s: number\n+  last_trigger_ts: number\n+  instrument: string | null\n+}\n+``​`\n+\n+`online` 由 `/mg/sys/heartbeat` 决定：3 秒内没有 heartbeat，前端所有 lane 进入 `OFFLINE`。lane 2-4 没有数据时显示 `WAITING`。\n+\n+## 调试 Tips\n+\n+抓 OSC mirror：\n+\n+``​`bash\n+python tools/osc_dump.py --port 5006\n+``​`\n+\n+检查后端快照：\n+\n+``​`bash\n+curl http://localhost:8000/api/lanes\n+``​`\n+\n+检查 WebSocket：\n+\n+``​`bash\n+python -c \"code = '''import asyncio, json, websockets\n+async def main():\n+    async with websockets.connect('ws://***REDACTED-IP***:8000/ws/lanes') as ws:\n+        print(json.dumps(json.loads(await ws.recv()), indent=2)[:1200])\n+asyncio.run(main())'''; 下面给出计划。

 I can see the user needs a layout with a shared header displaying the camera feed, and the Python pipeline is already set up to produce annotated frames with skeleton overlays through the webcam preview tool. I should integrate this with the FastAPI backend to stream those frames to the frontend.

My plan is to add an MJPEG endpoint on the backend that buffers frames, then have the Python tool POST encoded JPEG frames at around 10-15Hz to keep CPU usage reasonable. On the frontend, I'll create a new camera component that displays the stream via a simple `<img>` tag pointing to the MJPEG endpoint, then restructure the BigScreen layout to position this camera feed above the master HUD or in a dedicated top region. MJPEG is the cleanest approach here since browsers support it natively in image tags without needing WebSocket complexity.

For the Python side, I'll use `urllib.request` from the standard library to POST JPEG frames—no new dependencies needed. The backend will accept frames at `/api/video/frame`, store the latest one in memory, and serve it through the MJPEG stream. If frames stop arriving, I'll show a placeholder image to indicate the connection is stale.

Building the MJPEG streaming endpoint... I need to integrate the CameraStage component into the BigScreen view above the lanes, then verify the whole pipeline works end-to-end—either with a test script posting static frames or by running the actual webcam tool with the mirror flag enabled. The key design points are keeping bandwidth modest through 15Hz throttling and JPEG compression, handling multiple concurrent viewers through a shared buffer, and gracefully falling back to a placeholder when the stream goes idle.

浏览器收到 Content-Type=text/html 的响应，图片加载失败，摄像头被判定为离线。修复方案是在 vite.config.ts 的 proxy 配置中添加 `/video` 路径，然后重启 dev server 让代理生效。
